title: Payroll Calculator
spec: Write a function called `payroll(workers)` that takes a list of worker data strings. Each string has a type (hourly, salaried, freelance, or commissioned), a name, and two numbers. Parse these strings and create objects using distinct classes for an hourly employee, a salaried employee, a freelance contractor, and a commissioned worker. An hourly employee calculates pay as the first number (hours) times the second (rate). A salaried employee uses the first number (annual salary) divided by twelve, ignoring the second. A freelance contractor uses the first number (project fee) plus the second (bonus). A commissioned worker uses the first number (base) plus ten percent of the second (sales). The function should instantiate the appropriate class for each string, call a calculation method on each, and return a list of tuples containing the employee name and their calculated pay rounded to two decimals. Example input: ['hourly John 40 15.50', 'salaried Jane 60000 0']. Output: [('John', 620.0), ('Jane', 5000.0)].

title: Calculator Actions
spec: Write a function called `calculate(actions)` that computes a final value starting from zero based on a list of action tuples. Each tuple has an operation type and a number. Define distinct classes for an addition operation, a subtraction operation, a multiplication operation, and a division operation. An addition operation adds the number to the current total. A subtraction operation subtracts the number. A multiplication operation multiplies the total by the number. A division operation divides the total by the number, using integer division. Loop through the input list, instantiate the matching operation class for each tuple, apply its effect to the running total, and return the final integer total. Example input: [('add', 10), ('multiply', 3), ('subtract', 5)]. Output: 25.

title: Notification Router
spec: Write a function called `route(messages)` that takes a list of message tuples containing a destination type, an address, and a message body. Define separate classes for an email notification, a text message notification, a push notification, and a voice call notification. Each class should have a formatting method. An email notification prefixes the body with the word Subject. A text message notification truncates the body to exactly ten characters. A push notification wraps the body in square brackets. A voice call notification prefixes the body with the words Warning Message. Iterate through the input, instantiate the correct notification class for each message based on the destination type, and collect the formatted strings into a list. Return the list of formatted strings. Example input: [('email', 'admin', 'System down')]. Output: ['Subject System down'].

title: Combat Turn Processor
spec: Write a function called `combat(actions)` that processes a sequence of combat actions in a turn-based game. The input is a list of action strings. Parse these strings and represent them using distinct classes for a melee attack, a ranged attack, a healing spell, and a defensive block. Each class should have an execution method that applies its effect to a shared health integer starting at one hundred. A melee attack reduces health by ten. A ranged attack reduces health by five. A healing spell increases health by twenty. A defensive block adds fifteen to health to absorb damage. Instantiate the appropriate class for each action string and execute them in order. Return the final health value. Example input: ['ranged', 'block', 'melee', 'heal']. Output: 120.

title: Smart Home Sensors
spec: Write a function called `sensors(readings)` that analyzes a list of sensor reading tuples. Each tuple has a sensor type, a location, and a raw value. Model the sensors using different classes for a temperature sensor, a humidity sensor, a motion sensor, and a light sensor. The temperature sensor converts its value from Celsius to Fahrenheit by multiplying by one point eight and adding thirty two. The humidity sensor caps its percentage value at one hundred. The motion sensor translates a one or zero into a boolean True or False. The light sensor divides its lux value by ten. Instantiate the corresponding class for each tuple, process the raw value, and return a list of processed values. Example input: [('temperature', 'kitchen', 20), ('motion', 'hall', 1)]. Output: [68.0, True].

title: Area Calculator
spec: Write a function called `areas(shapes)` that computes the total area of a collection of geometric shapes. The input is a list of tuples where the first element is the shape name and the remaining elements are dimensions. Create specific classes for a circle shape, a rectangle shape, a triangle shape, and a square shape. The circle shape takes a radius and computes area as radius squared times three. The rectangle shape takes a width and height and multiplies them. The triangle shape takes a base and height, multiplies them, and divides by two. The square shape takes a single side length and squares it. Instantiate the proper class for each shape, call its area computation method, and return the sum of all areas as a float. Example input: [('circle', 10), ('square', 5)]. Output: 325.0.

title: System Audit Log
spec: Write a function called `audit(events)` that reads a list of system event strings. Represent different events with distinct classes for a login event, a logout event, a file read event, and a file write event. The input strings are formatted as the event type followed by a user name and a timestamp separated by spaces. A login event type is the word in. A logout event is out. A file read event is read. A file write event is write. Each class should extract and store the user name and timestamp from the split string. Process the input list by instantiating the correct event class for each string. Return a list of tuples containing the event class name description, the user name, and the timestamp. Example input: ['in Alice 1000', 'read Bob 1005']. Output: [('login', 'Alice', '1000'), ('read', 'Bob', '1005')].

title: Media Playlist Exporter
spec: Write a function called `playlist(items)` that formats a list of media items. The input is a list of tuples containing the media type and its two metadata elements. Define individual classes for a video file, an audio track, a podcast episode, and an image file. A video file formats as its title followed by its resolution. An audio track formats as its title followed by its artist. A podcast episode formats as its show name followed by its episode number. An image file formats as its title followed by its dimensions. Loop through the input, instantiate the suitable class for each item, and use a method on the class to generate the display string. Return the list of display strings. Example input: [('video', 'Intro', '1080p')]. Output: ['Intro 1080p'].

title: Highway Toll Calculator
spec: Write a function called `tolls(vehicles)` that calculates the toll fee for a line of vehicles. The input is a list of tuples containing the vehicle type, weight, and number of passengers. Use distinct classes to represent a passenger car, a delivery truck, a passenger bus, and a commercial van. A passenger car pays five plus one per passenger. A delivery truck pays ten plus two per thousand units of weight. A passenger bus pays fifteen flat. A commercial van pays eight plus one per thousand units of weight. For each tuple, instantiate the matching vehicle class, calculate its toll fee, and return the total sum of all fees collected. Example input: [('car', 1500, 2), ('bus', 5000, 20)]. Output: 22.

title: Kitchen Ticket Printer
spec: Write a function called `ticket(orders)` that generates a kitchen preparation ticket from a list of ordered items. The input is a list of tuples containing the item category and two details strings. Define specific classes for a main course, a side dish, a drink beverage, and a sweet dessert. A main course formats its meat and cooking temperature separated by a space. A side dish formats its vegetable and portion size separated by a space. A drink beverage formats its flavor and ice preference separated by a space. A sweet dessert formats its type and toppings separated by a space. Instantiate the appropriate class for each item based on its category, generate its preparation string, and return a single string with all preparation steps joined by a comma and a space. Example input: [('main', 'steak', 'rare'), ('side', 'peas', 'large')]. Output: 'steak rare, peas large'.

title: Freight Cost Estimator
spec: Write a function called `freight(cargo)` that estimates the shipping cost for a list of cargo items. The input is a list of tuples containing the transport method, distance, and weight. Implement separate classes for an air cargo shipment, a sea freight shipment, a rail transport shipment, and a road truck shipment. Air cargo costs ten times weight plus distance. Sea freight costs weight plus half the distance. Rail transport costs twice the weight plus distance. Road truck shipment costs five times weight plus twice the distance. Create the correct class instance for each cargo item, compute its cost, and return the total cost for the entire list. Example input: [('air', 100, 50), ('sea', 1000, 200)]. Output: 1300.0.

title: Network Traffic Analyzer
spec: Write a function called `analyze(packets)` that computes total payload sizes from a list of simulated network packets. The input is a list of tuples representing the protocol, header size, and total size. Define individual classes for a transmission control packet, a user datagram packet, an internet control packet, and a secure shell packet. The payload is calculated by subtracting the header size from the total size. For a secure shell packet, the payload is further reduced by an encryption padding of sixteen. For the other three packets, the payload is just the total size minus the header size. For each tuple, instantiate the correct packet class based on the protocol, calculate its payload, and return a list of these payload sizes. Example input: [('tcp', 20, 100), ('ssh', 20, 100)]. Output: [80, 64].

title: Shopping Cart Discounts
spec: Write a function called `checkout(cart)` that applies various discounts to a starting cart total. The input is a tuple where the first element is a float representing the initial total and the second element is a list of discount tuples containing the discount type and a value. Create distinct classes for a percentage discount, a fixed amount discount, a tiered discount, and a seasonal discount. A percentage discount reduces the total by its percentage value. A fixed amount discount subtracts its amount directly. A tiered discount removes ten if the total is over one hundred, or removes its value otherwise. A seasonal discount reduces the total by twenty percent if its associated string value is winter. Instantiate the correct discount class for each tuple and apply them sequentially to the total. Return the final total. Example input: (200.0, [('percentage', 10), ('fixed', 15)]). Output: 165.0.

title: Account Ledger
spec: Write a function called `ledger(transactions)` that processes a list of bank transactions and computes the final balance starting from zero. The input is a list of tuples with the transaction type and amount. Use separate classes to model a cash deposit, a check withdrawal, a wire transfer, and an overdraft fee. A cash deposit adds its amount. A check withdrawal subtracts its amount. A wire transfer subtracts its amount plus a fee of fifteen. An overdraft fee subtracts thirty five regardless of the amount provided. Iterate over the input, create the corresponding transaction class instance, apply its effect to the balance, and return the final balance. Example input: [('deposit', 1000), ('wire', 200)]. Output: 785.

title: Document Generator
spec: Write a function called `generate(components)` that builds a text document from a list of structural components. The input is a list of tuples specifying the component type and its text content. Define classes for a title header, a paragraph block, a block quote, and a code snippet. A title header capitalizes all text and appends five equal signs separated by a space. A paragraph block simply returns the text. A block quote prefixes the text with an angle bracket and a space. A code snippet wraps the text in backticks. Instantiate the appropriate class for each component, generate its formatted string, and return a list of all formatted strings. Example input: [('title', 'hello')]. Output: ['HELLO ====='].

title: Disk Space Calculator
spec: Write a function called `disk(nodes)` that calculates the total disk space used by a simulated file system structure. The input is a list of tuples containing a node type and its size attribute. Create separate classes to represent a regular file, a directory folder, a symbolic link, and a compressed archive. A regular file uses its exact given size. A directory folder ignores the size attribute and uses a fixed overhead of four thousand and ninety six. A symbolic link ignores the size and uses a fixed size of sixty four. A compressed archive takes its given size and multiplies it by point eight. Instantiate the correct class for each node, determine its space usage, and return the total space used as a float. Example input: [('file', 1000), ('folder', 0)]. Output: 5096.0.

title: Access Control System
spec: Write a function called `access(request)` that determines if a user has sufficient rights based on a list of assigned roles. The input is a tuple containing a required clearance integer and a list of role tuples. Each role tuple has a role category and its base level. Model the roles using classes for an administrator role, a manager role, a staff role, and a guest role. An administrator role has a clearance equal to its base level plus fifty. A manager role adds twenty to its base level. A staff role uses its exact base level. A guest role always has a clearance of one regardless of the base level. Instantiate the respective role classes for the user. Return a boolean indicating whether the highest clearance among all the user roles meets or exceeds the required clearance. Example input: (30, [('staff', 15), ('manager', 15)]). Output: True.

title: Power Consumption Tracker
spec: Write a function called `power(devices)` that calculates the total daily energy used by various smart devices. The input is a list of tuples with the device category, active hours, and standby hours. Define classes for a smart television, a smart refrigerator, a smart thermostat, and a smart speaker. A smart television uses one hundred watts active and five watts standby. A smart refrigerator uses fifty watts active and twenty watts standby. A smart thermostat uses ten watts active and two watts standby. A smart speaker uses fifteen watts active and one watt standby. Instantiate the correct device class for each tuple, calculate its total watt-hours for the day by multiplying hours by respective wattages and summing them, and return the sum across all devices. Example input: [('tv', 4, 20), ('thermostat', 24, 0)]. Output: 740.

title: RPG Character Stats
spec: Write a function called `stats(equipment)` that calculates the total armor class of a character based on their equipped items. The input is a list of tuples detailing the equipment slot and base defense. Implement distinct classes for a head helmet, a chest plate, a leg guard, and a shield offhand. A head helmet contributes its base defense plus two. A chest plate contributes double its base defense. A leg guard contributes its base defense plus one. A shield offhand contributes its base defense plus a block bonus of five. Instantiate the appropriate equipment class for each item, aggregate the total defense value, and return it. Example input: [('chest', 10), ('shield', 5)]. Output: 30.

title: MIDI Event Parser
spec: Write a function called `sequencer(events)` that processes a stream of musical events to find the highest note played. The input is a list of tuples with the event type, note number, and velocity. Create separate classes for a note on event, a note off event, a pitch bend event, and a control change event. Each class must implement a method that returns the active note number if it represents a newly played note, or negative one otherwise. A note on event returns its note number if its velocity is greater than zero, or negative one otherwise. The other three events always return negative one regardless of input. Instantiate the corresponding event class for each tuple, call its method, and return the maximum active note number found. Return negative one if there are none. Example input: [('on', 60, 100), ('off', 60, 0), ('on', 64, 0)]. Output: 60.

title: Meal Nutrition Calculator
spec: Write a function called `nutrition(ingredients)` that computes the total calories for a recipe. The input is a list of tuples containing the ingredient category, weight in grams, and calories per gram. Implement specific classes for a meat ingredient, a vegetable ingredient, a dairy ingredient, and a grain ingredient. A meat ingredient adds a preparation penalty of fifty calories to its base calories of weight times calories per gram. A vegetable ingredient subtracts ten calories from its base calories for digestion. A dairy ingredient multiplies its base calories by one point one. A grain ingredient uses its exact base calories. Instantiate the proper ingredient class for each item, calculate its adjusted calories, and return the sum of all calories rounded to the nearest whole number. Example input: [('meat', 200, 2), ('vegetable', 100, 0.5)]. Output: 490.

title: Issue Tracker Triage
spec: Write a function called `triage(issues)` that calculates the priority score of software issues. The input is a list of tuples containing the issue type, base severity, and number of affected users. Use separate classes for a crash bug, a user interface glitch, a feature request, and a security vulnerability. A crash bug multiplies severity by affected users. A user interface glitch uses just the base severity. A feature request divides affected users by ten and adds the severity. A security vulnerability squares the base severity and adds one thousand. Instantiate the matching issue class for each tuple, compute its priority score, and return a list of scores in the same order. Example input: [('crash', 5, 100), ('ui', 3, 50)]. Output: [500, 3].

title: Deployment Workflow
spec: Write a function called `deploy(steps)` that simulates a software deployment process. The input is a list of step tuples containing the step category and duration in minutes. Model the workflow using classes for an automated test step, a build compilation step, a manual approval step, and a server rollout step. An automated test step adds two minutes of setup time to its duration. A build compilation step adds a ten percent overhead to its duration. A manual approval step always ignores its given duration and takes exactly fourteen hundred and forty minutes. A server rollout step uses its exact given duration. Instantiate the correct step class for each item, calculate the actual time taken by calling a method on it, and return the total time for the entire workflow. Example input: [('test', 10), ('build', 20)]. Output: 34.0.

title: Celestial Body Mass
spec: Write a function called `astronomy(bodies)` that estimates the total mass of a system of celestial objects. The input is a list of tuples with the body type, radius, and base density. Create specific classes for a rocky planet, a gas giant, a dwarf star, and an asteroid rock. A rocky planet multiplies its volume by its density. A gas giant uses half its density when multiplying by volume. A dwarf star uses ten times its density when multiplying by volume. An asteroid rock ignores volume and just returns its radius times density. Assume volume is radius cubed for this estimation. Instantiate the appropriate body class for each tuple, calculate its estimated mass, and return the sum of all masses. Example input: [('rocky', 2, 5), ('asteroid', 10, 2)]. Output: 60.

title: Weather Forecaster
spec: Write a function called `forecast(days)` that generates a summary of daily weather conditions. The input is a list of tuples with the condition type, high temperature, and low temperature. Define individual classes for a sunny day, a rainy day, a snowy day, and a cloudy day. A sunny day reports clear skies and the high temperature. A rainy day reports precipitation and the average of the high and low. A snowy day reports freezing and the low temperature. A cloudy day reports overcast and the difference between high and low. Instantiate the correct condition class for each day, ask it for its summary string by combining the description and the calculated number separated by a space, and return a list of these strings. Example input: [('sunny', 30, 20), ('rainy', 20, 10)]. Output: ['clear skies 30', 'precipitation 15.0'].

title: Space Fleet Simulator
spec: Write a function `simulate(fleet)` that takes a list of tuples containing a vessel category string and a numeric stat. Model the vessels using distinct object structures for a cargo ship, an escort fighter, a medical frigate, and an exploration rover. A cargo ship adds its stat to total capacity. An escort fighter adds its stat multiplied by 5 to fleet defense. A medical frigate adds half its stat to fleet defense and half to capacity. An exploration rover adds its stat to both capacity and defense. Use a dictionary to map the string categories to their corresponding object structures before processing the list. Instantiate the appropriate structures, process them, and return a tuple of total capacity and total defense. An input pairing cargo ship with 10, and escort fighter with 2 returns 10 capacity and 10 defense.

title: Text Adventure Equipment
spec: Write a function `equip(inventory)` that processes a list of equipment strings paired with power integers. Model the items as distinct structures for a magic weapon, a heavy armor, a healing potion, and a speed ring. A magic weapon increases attack by the power plus 2. A heavy armor increases defense by the power but reduces attack by 1. A healing potion adds to health but disappears after boosting health by its power multiplied by 10. A speed ring adds its power equally to attack, defense, and health. Map the equipment strings to their respective object structures using a dictionary before calculating the totals. Instantiate the proper items, sum their effects, and return a list with total attack, defense, and health. An input pairing magic weapon with 3, and heavy armor with 4 returns 4 for attack, 4 for defense, and 0 for health.

title: Public Transit Router
spec: Write a function `route(stops)` that calculates transit times from a list of transport modes and distance values. Model the network using separate structures for a bus stop, a train station, a ferry terminal, and a bicycle share. A bus stop takes distance multiplied by 3 minutes plus a 2 minute wait. A train station takes distance multiplied by 1 minute plus a 5 minute wait. A ferry terminal takes distance multiplied by 4 minutes plus a 15 minute wait. A bicycle share takes distance multiplied by 2 minutes with no wait. Create a registry dictionary linking the transport mode names to their corresponding structures before evaluating the list. Instantiate the structures, compute the individual times, and return the total travel time. An input pairing bus stop with 5, and train station with 10 returns 32 minutes.

title: Escape Room Puzzle
spec: Write a function `solve(steps)` that processes a sequence of puzzle interaction tuples containing an object type and a difficulty rating. Use distinct structures for a locked door, a floor switch, a hidden clue, and a laser grid. A locked door requires twice its difficulty in seconds to pick. A floor switch takes exactly 10 seconds regardless of difficulty. A hidden clue requires its difficulty squared in seconds to decipher. A laser grid takes 20 seconds minus its difficulty. Associate the object type strings with their structures using a dictionary map before calculating the time. Instantiate the puzzle objects to calculate the time spent on each step and return the total seconds needed to escape. An input pairing locked door with 3, and hidden clue with 4 takes 22 seconds.

title: Factory Assembly Line
spec: Write a function `manufacture(tasks)` to compute the energy cost of production steps given as pairs of operation names and duration integers. Represent the machines as individual structures for a welding robot, a painting station, a quality scanner, and a packaging belt. A welding robot consumes 15 energy units per duration unit plus a base of 50. A painting station consumes 5 units per duration unit. A quality scanner always consumes exactly 20 units. A packaging belt consumes 2 units per duration plus a base of 10. Use a dictionary to link the operation names to their specific machine structures before evaluating the sequence. Create the corresponding machine representations, evaluate the sequence, and return the total energy consumed. An input pairing painting station with 10, and quality scanner with 5 uses 70 energy.

title: Zoo Enclosure Planner
spec: Write a function `plan(animals)` to determine the total daily food requirements from a list of species categories and weight integers. Use separate object models for a carnivore beast, a gentle herbivore, an avian flyer, and an aquatic swimmer. A carnivore beast eats its weight multiplied by 0.05 in meat. A gentle herbivore eats its weight multiplied by 0.1 in plants. An avian flyer eats a flat 2 units of seeds plus its weight multiplied by 0.01. An aquatic swimmer eats its weight multiplied by 0.08 in fish. Map the species categories to their respective animal structures using a dictionary before computing the diet. Instantiate the animal models, calculate their diets, and return the sum of all food units needed. An input pairing carnivore beast with 200, and avian flyer with 50 returns 12.5 units.

title: Fantasy Tavern Generator
spec: Write a function `populate(visitors)` to calculate the total gold spent by patrons, given a list of character roles and their starting wealth. Model the patrons using distinct structures for a quest giver, a shady merchant, a weary traveler, and a local drunk. A quest giver spends exactly 10 percent of their wealth. A shady merchant spends nothing but instead subtracts 5 gold from the tavern earnings. A weary traveler spends all their wealth up to a maximum of 20 gold. A local drunk spends exactly 2 gold regardless of their wealth. Create a dictionary mapping the role strings to their corresponding patron structures before processing the visitors. Create the patron structures, apply their behaviors in order, and return the tavern net earnings. An input pairing quest giver with 50, and weary traveler with 30 yields 25 gold.

title: Theme Park Queue Manager
spec: Write a function `admit(guests)` to calculate thrill points generated by riders, provided as pairs of ride types and rider ages. Model the attractions as separate structures for a roller coaster, a water flume, a haunted house, and a gentle carousel. A roller coaster yields 50 thrill points if the age is over 12, otherwise 0. A water flume yields 20 points for any age. A haunted house yields 30 points but subtracts 10 if the rider is under 10 years old. A gentle carousel yields a flat 10 points for any age. Link the ride type strings to their attraction structures using a dictionary registry before evaluating the guests. Instantiate the attraction models for each guest, tally the points, and return the total. An input pairing roller coaster with 14, and haunted house with 8 returns 70 points.

title: Garden Layout Planner
spec: Write a function `plant(seeds)` to calculate the total water required for a garden, given a list of plant categories and area sizes. Represent the vegetation using distinct models for a root vegetable, a vine crop, a fruit tree, and a desert succulent. A root vegetable needs 2 liters per area unit. A vine crop needs 3 liters per area plus a flat 5 liters for soil prep. A fruit tree needs 10 liters per area unit. A desert succulent needs exactly 1 liter flat regardless of area size. Map the plant categories to their corresponding structures using a dictionary before calculating the water needs. Create the corresponding plant structures, compute their individual needs, and return the grand total of water in liters. An input pairing root vegetable with 10, and vine crop with 4 requires 37 liters.

title: Real Estate Portfolio
spec: Write a function `evaluate(properties)` to determine the total annual tax from a list of property types and base values. Model the real estate using separate structures for a residential apartment, a commercial storefront, a vacant lot, and an industrial warehouse. A residential apartment is taxed at 1 percent of its value. A commercial storefront is taxed at 3 percent of its value plus a flat fee of 500. A vacant lot is taxed at 0.5 percent of its value. An industrial warehouse is taxed at a flat 2 percent. Use a dictionary to associate the property types with their structures before computing the total tax. Instantiate the property models, compute the taxes, and return the total amount. An input pairing residential apartment with 100000, and vacant lot with 50000 returns 1250.

title: Board Game Scoring
spec: Write a function `score(cards)` to calculate final victory points from a player hand, given as pairs of card types and face values. Model the components as distinct structures for a resource card, a development card, a victory point card, and a penalty card. A resource card is worth 0 points. A development card is worth 1 point plus an extra point if its face value exceeds 5. A victory point card is worth exactly its face value. A penalty card subtracts 2 points from the score. Map the card type strings directly to their component structures using a dictionary before evaluating the hand. Create the card structures, evaluate each, and return the total score. An input pairing development card with 6, and penalty card with 3 returns 0 points.

title: Traffic Intersection Control
spec: Write a function `regulate(events)` to compute the total seconds a vehicle must wait, given a sequence of intersection elements and an arrival timestamp. Represent the elements using individual structures for a traffic light, a stop sign, a pedestrian crossing, and a toll booth. A traffic light adds 30 seconds if the arrival timestamp is even, otherwise 0. A stop sign always adds exactly 5 seconds. A pedestrian crossing adds 10 seconds if the timestamp is a multiple of 3. A toll booth always adds 15 seconds flat. Create a dictionary linking the element strings to their control structures before processing the sequence. Instantiate the control structures to process the sequence and return the total wait time. An input of timestamp 12 with a traffic light and a stop sign yields 35 seconds.

title: Medieval Castle Defenses
spec: Write a function `defend(attacks)` to determine the remaining integrity of a fortress after a siege, starting from 1000 points, given a list of defense types and incoming damage amounts. Model the fortifications using separate structures for a stone wall, a wooden gate, a water moat, and a magical barrier. A stone wall reduces incoming damage by half before subtracting it from integrity. A wooden gate takes full damage but ignores any hit under 20 points. A water moat takes no damage but reduces integrity by 10 for every attack. A magical barrier ignores the attack entirely but reduces integrity by a flat 5 points. Map the defense types to their corresponding structures using a dictionary before applying the incoming damage. Create the defense structures, apply the attacks, and return the final integrity. An input pairing stone wall with 50, and magical barrier with 100 leaves 970 integrity.

title: Music Festival Lineup
spec: Write a function `schedule(performers)` to calculate the total stage setup time required for a concert, given a list of act genres and their set lengths in minutes. Represent the acts using distinct structures for a rock band, an acoustic soloist, an electronic dj, and a comedy act. A rock band requires 30 minutes of setup regardless of set length. An acoustic soloist needs 5 minutes. An electronic dj needs 10 minutes plus 1 extra minute for every 10 minutes of their set length. A comedy act requires exactly 2 minutes of setup. Associate the genre strings with their act structures using a dictionary registry before determining the setup times. Instantiate the acts, determine their setup times, and return the sum. An input pairing rock band with 60, and electronic dj with 50 requires 45 minutes.

title: E-commerce Shipping Bins
spec: Write a function `pack(items)` to calculate the total shipping cost from a list of container types and item weights in ounces. Model the packaging using individual structures for a bubble mailer, a cardboard box, a wooden crate, and a plastic polybag. A bubble mailer costs 2 dollars plus 10 cents per ounce. A cardboard box costs 5 dollars plus 5 cents per ounce. A wooden crate costs 20 dollars flat, regardless of weight. A plastic polybag costs 1 dollar plus 20 cents per ounce. Use a dictionary to link the container types to their respective packaging structures before calculating the costs. Create the container models, compute the cost for each shipment, and return the total dollars. An input pairing bubble mailer with 10, and wooden crate with 500 costs 23 dollars.

title: Dungeon Trap Processor
spec: Write a function `trigger(steps)` to calculate total damage taken by an adventurer walking through a corridor, given a list of trap varieties and severity levels. Use separate structures for a poison dart, a spiked pit, a fire rune, and a swinging blade. A poison dart deals its severity in damage immediately plus 2 points of lingering damage. A spiked pit deals its severity squared in damage. A fire rune deals 10 points of damage if severity is greater than 3, otherwise 0. A swinging blade deals exactly 5 damage regardless of severity. Map the trap varieties to their object structures using a dictionary before accumulating the damage. Instantiate the trap models, calculate the damage from each, and return the total. An input pairing poison dart with 2, and spiked pit with 3 deals 13 damage.

title: Hotel Room Booking
spec: Write a function `book(requests)` to compute the total revenue for a night, given a list of room categories and the number of occupants. Represent the accommodations using distinct structures for an economy room, a standard suite, a luxury penthouse, and a capsule bed. An economy room charges 50 dollars plus 10 dollars per occupant. A standard suite charges 100 dollars flat for up to 4 occupants, ignoring extra people. A luxury penthouse charges 300 dollars plus 50 dollars for every occupant beyond 2. A capsule bed charges 20 dollars flat per occupant. Create a registry dictionary associating the room categories with their structures before evaluating the revenue. Create the room structures, evaluate the revenue, and return the sum. An input pairing economy room with 2, and capsule bed with 1 returns 90 dollars.

title: Bakery Recipe Scaler
spec: Write a function `scale(ingredients)` to determine the total grams of materials needed for a large batch, given a list of ingredient classifications and base weights. Model the recipe components as separate structures for a dry powder, a liquid extract, a fresh garnish, and a sticky syrup. A dry powder weight is multiplied by 3. A liquid extract weight is multiplied by 2. A fresh garnish weight remains exactly the same. A sticky syrup weight is multiplied by 1.5. Map the ingredient classifications to their corresponding structures using a dictionary before processing the batch. Instantiate the ingredient structures to process the base weights and return the final total weight in grams. An input pairing dry powder with 100, and fresh garnish with 50 yields 350 grams.

title: Asteroid Mining Yield
spec: Write a function `mine(targets)` to calculate the total credits earned from an expedition, given a list of asteroid compositions and extracted tons. Use individual object models for an ice asteroid, an iron asteroid, a precious metal asteroid, and a rocky debris. An ice asteroid yields 10 credits per ton. An iron asteroid yields 50 credits per ton but deducts a 100 credit flat extraction fee. A precious metal asteroid yields 500 credits per ton but halves the tons before calculating. A rocky debris yields exactly 0 credits. Use a dictionary to link the composition strings to their asteroid structures before computing the credits. Create the asteroid structures, compute the net credits, and return the total. An input pairing ice asteroid with 20, and precious metal asteroid with 4 returns 1200 credits.

title: Fitness Workout Generator
spec: Write a function `train(routines)` to compute the total calories burned, given a sequence of exercise types and duration in minutes. Model the activities using distinct structures for a cardio sprint, a strength lift, a flexibility stretch, and a balance pose. A cardio sprint burns 15 calories per minute. A strength lift burns 8 calories per minute plus a flat 20 calories for muscle repair. A flexibility stretch burns 3 calories per minute. A balance pose burns exactly 1 calorie per minute. Map the exercise types to their activity structures using a dictionary before calculating the total burned. Instantiate the exercise structures to calculate the energy expenditure and return the total burned. An input pairing cardio sprint with 10, and strength lift with 5 burns 210 calories.

title: Art Gallery Curation
spec: Write a function `curate(pieces)` to calculate the total insurance premium for an exhibition, given a list of art mediums and appraisal values. Represent the artworks using separate structures for an oil painting, a marble sculpture, a digital installation, and a charcoal sketch. An oil painting premium is 2 percent of its value. A marble sculpture premium is 1 percent of its value plus a 50 dollar handling fee. A digital installation has a flat premium of 100 dollars regardless of value. A charcoal sketch premium is a flat 10 dollars. Create a dictionary mapping the art mediums to their respective artwork structures before determining the premiums. Create the artwork structures, determine the premiums, and return the grand total. An input pairing oil painting with 1000, and digital installation with 5000 yields 120 dollars.

title: Farm Animal Feeding
spec: Write a function `feed(livestock)` to calculate the total pounds of feed consumed daily, given a list of animal roles and their ages in months. Model the herd using distinct structures for a dairy cow, a wool sheep, an egg chicken, and a guard dog. A dairy cow eats 20 pounds plus 1 pound for every month of age. A wool sheep eats 10 pounds flat. An egg chicken eats 2 pounds if under 6 months old, and 3 pounds if older. A guard dog eats 5 pounds plus 2 pounds per month of age. Associate the animal roles with their structures using a dictionary registry before tallying the consumption. Instantiate the livestock structures, tally the individual consumptions, and return the total pounds. An input pairing dairy cow with 12, and wool sheep with 20 requires 42 pounds.

title: Library Book Categorization
spec: Write a function `catalog(books)` to determine the total shelf space needed in centimeters, given a list of publication genres and page counts. Use separate structures for a fiction novel, a reference manual, a graphic magazine, and a pocket dictionary. A fiction novel takes 1 centimeter per 100 pages. A reference manual takes 2 centimeters per 100 pages plus 1 extra centimeter for its hard cover. A graphic magazine always takes exactly 0.5 centimeters regardless of page count. A pocket dictionary takes exactly 2 centimeters flat. Map the publication genres to their structures using a dictionary before computing the shelf space. Create the publication structures, compute the widths, and return the total space. An input pairing fiction novel with 300, and reference manual with 400 takes 12 centimeters.

title: Car Wash Bay Assigner
spec: Write a function `wash(cars)` to calculate the total gallons of water used by a facility, given a list of service packages and vehicle dirtiness levels from 1 to 10. Represent the services using individual structures for a basic rinse, a soap scrub, a premium detail, and a tire scrub. A basic rinse uses 10 gallons plus the dirtiness level. A soap scrub uses 20 gallons plus twice the dirtiness level. A premium detail uses 50 gallons flat, completely ignoring the dirtiness level. A tire scrub uses 5 gallons plus the dirtiness level. Use a dictionary to link the service packages to their wash structures before calculating the water usage. Instantiate the service structures, compute the water usage for each, and return the total. An input pairing basic rinse with 5, and premium detail with 8 uses 65 gallons.

title: Magical Alchemy Brewer
spec: Write a function `brew(ingredients)` to determine the final potency of a potion, given a list of component types and their raw mana values. Model the components using distinct structures for a volatile herb, a crystal dust, a monster essence, and a pure water. A volatile herb adds its mana multiplied by 2. A crystal dust adds its mana but also provides a flat bonus of 5 potency. A monster essence triples its mana but subtracts 10 potency due to toxicity. A pure water adds exactly 1 potency regardless of mana. Create a dictionary mapping the component types to their structures before accumulating the final potency. Create the component structures, accumulate the potency, and return the final integer value. An input pairing volatile herb with 3, and pure water with 4 returns 7.

title: Airline Baggage Calculator
spec: Write a function `calculate(passengers)` that takes a list of passenger data tuples containing passenger name, loyalty tier, and a list of bag weights. Design small classes to represent a passenger profile, a checked bag, and a baggage policy. The baggage policy charges fifty dollars for a bag under twenty kilos, and one hundred dollars for heavier bags. A passenger profile should calculate its own total by creating checked bag instances and applying the policy, with the elite loyalty tier getting one bag free. Return a list of tuples with passenger name and total fee. Example input: a list with one tuple of a passenger named Alice, basic tier, and bags weighing fifteen and twenty five kilos. Expected output: a list with a tuple for Alice and one hundred fifty dollars.

title: Insurance Claim Assessor
spec: Write a function `assess(claims)` that processes a list of raw claim tuples containing policyholder name, incident type, and repair cost. Solve this by defining classes for a policy holder, a damage claim, and a payout calculator. The damage claim should encapsulate the incident type and cost. The payout calculator approves full repair cost for natural disasters, and half cost for collisions. The policy holder should aggregate their damage claims and compute the total payout. Return a list of names and approved payout amounts. Example: a list with a tuple for Bob, collision, and two thousand. Output: a list with a tuple for Bob and one thousand.

title: University Credit Auditor
spec: Write a function `audit(students)` that takes a list of student data containing name, major, and a list of completed course tuples holding the course code, credits, and grade. Use small classes to represent a student record, a course enrollment, and a degree program. The course enrollment should store the code, credits, and grade, computing earned credits only if the grade is C or higher. The degree program specifies that a major requires forty total earned credits. The student record should use these classes to determine if the student is ready to graduate. Return a list of names of students who are ready to graduate. Example input: a list with a tuple for Carol, physics, and a list of courses totaling forty credits all with A grades. Output: a list containing Carol.

title: Emergency Room Triage
spec: Write a function `triage(patients)` that receives a list of tuples containing patient name, age, and a list of symptom severity scores. Model this using classes for a patient record, a vital sign reading, and a triage queue. A vital sign reading calculates a risk level: high if any symptom score is above eight, medium if above five, else low. The patient record should hold the name and vital sign readings, and determine priority where seniors over sixty five with high risk are top priority. The triage queue should sort patient records accordingly. Return a list of patient names in order of processing priority. Example: a list with a senior patient with high risk and a young patient with low risk. Output: a list with the senior patient first.

title: Fleet Maintenance Checker
spec: Write a function `check(vehicles)` receiving a list of vehicle tuples containing the license plate, vehicle type, and current mileage. Define classes for a delivery truck, a service log, and a maintenance schedule. The service log tracks the mileage. The maintenance schedule requires a service every ten thousand miles for vans and every fifteen thousand miles for sedans. The delivery truck class should combine the service log and maintenance schedule to flag if a vehicle is due for service, assuming last service was at zero miles. Return a list of license plates for vehicles needing immediate maintenance. Example: a list with a van at twelve thousand miles. Output: a list with the van license plate.

title: Software Seat Allocation
spec: Write a function `allocate(requests)` that processes a list of tuple requests containing company name, requested seats, and subscription type. Create classes for a corporate client, a software license, and a billing cycle. The software license should grant ten seats for a basic subscription and fifty for an enterprise one. The corporate client should store the requests and use the software license to determine if the requested seats exceed the granted amount. The billing cycle calculates the monthly fee based on allocated seats. Return a list of tuples with company name and a boolean indicating if they exceeded their limit. Example: a list with a basic subscription requesting twelve seats. Output: a list with the company name and true.

title: Conference Session Builder
spec: Write a function `schedule(sessions)` taking a list of tuples containing speaker name, topic, and duration in minutes. Use classes representing a conference speaker, a presentation slot, and a track schedule. The presentation slot stores the duration and topic. The track schedule organizes slots into morning and afternoon blocks, allowing up to one hundred eighty minutes per block. The conference speaker associates the name with their presentation slot. Build a track schedule by adding slots in order until a block is full, then move to the next. Return a list of speaker names successfully scheduled in the morning block. Example: three speakers with sixty minute duration each. Output: a list of the three speaker names.

title: Cinema Ticket Pricing
spec: Write a function `calculate(patrons)` that takes a list of tuples containing patron name, age, and movie format. Create classes for a movie patron, a cinema ticket, and a concession discount. The cinema ticket sets the base price at fifteen for standard and twenty for imax. The movie patron applies a senior discount of five off if the age is over sixty. The concession discount offers free popcorn if the ticket price after discount is greater than eighteen. Return a list of patron names who get free popcorn. Example: a list with a thirty year old seeing an imax movie. Output: a list with their name.

title: Produce Shelf Restock
spec: Write a function `restock(deliveries)` taking a list of delivery tuples with item name, category, and quantity received. Design classes for a grocery item, a store shelf, and an inventory manager. The grocery item holds the name and category. The store shelf has a maximum capacity of fifty items for produce and one hundred for dry goods. The inventory manager tracks items on the shelves, adding new deliveries and calculating the overflow if the quantity exceeds shelf capacity. Return a list of tuples with item name and the overflow amount. Example: a delivery of sixty apples in the produce category. Output: a list with apples and an overflow of ten.

title: Fitness Club Billing
spec: Write a function `invoice(members)` processing a list of tuples with member name, plan type, and locker rented. Model the solution with classes for a club member, a subscription plan, and a monthly invoice. The subscription plan costs fifty for basic and eighty for premium. The club member links to a subscription plan and tracks locker rental, which adds a flat twenty. The monthly invoice computes the final total, applying a ten percent discount on the subscription if premium is chosen. Return a list of tuples with member name and final billed amount. Example: a premium member with a locker. Output: a list with their name and ninety two.

title: Museum Tour Scheduler
spec: Write a function `schedule(groups)` that accepts a list of visitor group tuples containing group name, size, and preferred language. Create classes for a visitor group, a guided tour, and a museum gallery. The guided tour has a maximum capacity of twenty people and is conducted in a specific language. The museum gallery hosts multiple guided tours. Assign visitor groups to the earliest available guided tour in their language that has enough remaining capacity. Return a list of tuples with group name and the assigned tour language. Example: a French group of five people. Output: a list with the group name and French.

title: Mail Parcel Routing
spec: Write a function `route(parcels)` taking a list of tuples containing tracking number, destination zone, and weight. Use classes for a mail parcel, a shipping zone, and a delivery truck. The shipping zone determines transit time where zone one is local and takes one day, and zone two takes three days. The mail parcel holds the weight and tracking number. The delivery truck can carry up to five hundred weight units. Load mail parcels into the delivery truck until full, prioritizing zone one parcels. Return a list of tracking numbers successfully loaded onto the first delivery truck. Example: a local parcel weighing fifty and a zone two parcel weighing four hundred. Output: a list with the local parcel tracking number.

title: Interview Round Assigner
spec: Write a function `assign(candidates)` that receives a list of tuples containing candidate name, role applied for, and assessment score. Design classes for a job candidate, an interview panel, and a hiring pipeline. The interview panel requires a score above eighty for engineering roles and above seventy for sales roles to grant an interview. The job candidate encapsulates the name and score. The hiring pipeline uses the interview panel to evaluate all candidates and generates a schedule. Return a list of names of candidates who proceed to the interview panel. Example: an engineering candidate with a score of eighty five. Output: a list with that candidate name.

title: Aquarium Feeding Planner
spec: Write a function `plan(tanks)` processing a list of tuples with tank identifier, fish species, and population count. Create classes for a fish tank, a daily diet, and a feeding schedule. The daily diet requires two units of food per fish for sharks and one unit for all other species. The fish tank stores the population and species. The feeding schedule aggregates the fish tanks and calculates the total food units required for the entire facility per day. Return the total required food units as a single number. Example: a tank with five sharks and a tank with ten guppies. Output: twenty.

title: Campsite Booking Manager
spec: Write a function `book(requests)` accepting a list of tuples containing camper name, site preference, and duration in nights. Model the system with classes for a nature camper, a tent site, and a booking ledger. The tent site can either be premium with electricity or basic. The nature camper holds the name and preference. The booking ledger assigns available premium sites first if preferred, otherwise basic sites. The cost is thirty per night for premium and fifteen for basic. Return a list of tuples with camper name and total cost for their stay. Example: a camper staying two nights at a basic site. Output: a list with their name and thirty.

title: Ski Pass Generator
spec: Write a function `issue(skiers)` that processes a list of tuples with skier name, age, and days skiing. Use classes for a winter skier, a lift pass, and a gear rental. The lift pass costs eighty per day, but children under twelve pay fifty. The winter skier stores the age and name. The gear rental adds an optional thirty per day if the days skiing is less than three, assuming they do not own gear for short trips. Generate a lift pass for each winter skier and sum the costs. Return a list of tuples with skier name and total price. Example: an adult skiing for two days. Output: a list with the name and two hundred twenty.

title: Vehicle Policy Quoter
spec: Write a function `quote(drivers)` taking a list of tuples with driver name, years of experience, and car value. Design classes for a licensed driver, a vehicle profile, and an insurance policy. The vehicle profile calculates a base premium as five percent of the car value. The licensed driver adds a penalty where experience under three years adds five hundred to the premium. The insurance policy aggregates these details to compute the final annual quote. Return a list of tuples with driver name and the final quote amount. Example: a new driver with one year experience and a car valued at ten thousand. Output: a list with the name and one thousand.

title: Auction Bid Evaluator
spec: Write a function `evaluate(bids)` that accepts a list of tuples containing bidder name, item identifier, and bid amount. Use classes for an auction item, a user bid, and a winning ledger. The auction item has a starting price of one hundred. The user bid captures the bidder name and amount. The winning ledger tracks the highest valid user bid for each auction item, ignoring bids below the starting price. Return a list of tuples with item identifier and the winning bidder name. Example: an item with bids of ninety by Dave and one hundred twenty by Eve. Output: a list with the item identifier and Eve.

title: Wedding Table Assigner
spec: Write a function `seat(guests)` that processes a list of tuples with guest name, side of family, and dietary requirement. Model this using classes for a wedding guest, a banquet table, and a seating plan. The banquet table holds up to eight wedding guests. The seating plan must group guests by the side of the family into different banquet tables. The wedding guest holds the name and diet. Calculate how many vegetarian meals are needed for each side of the family. Return a list of tuples with side of family and the vegetarian meal count. Example: a bride side guest who is vegetarian. Output: a list with bride side and one.

title: Vet Clinic Scheduler
spec: Write a function `schedule(pets)` taking a list of tuples with pet name, animal type, and illness severity out of ten. Create classes for a clinic patient, a vet appointment, and a daily roster. The clinic patient captures the animal details. The vet appointment allocates thirty minutes for severity over five, and fifteen minutes otherwise. The daily roster keeps track of total scheduled minutes, up to a maximum of four hundred eighty minutes per day. Schedule the clinic patients in order and return a list of pet names that successfully get a vet appointment today. Example: a dog with severity eight. Output: a list with the dog name.

title: Energy Grid Balancer
spec: Write a function `balance(sources)` that takes a list of tuples containing plant name, energy type, and current output in megawatts. Define classes for a power source, a storage battery, and a grid controller. The power source models the plant generation. The storage battery has a capacity of five hundred megawatts. The grid controller distributes generated energy by sending the first thousand megawatts directly to the city, and routing any excess from solar or wind to the storage battery. Return a tuple containing the city energy supplied and the storage battery charge level. Example: a solar plant outputting twelve hundred. Output: a tuple of one thousand and two hundred.

title: Coffee Roast Evaluator
spec: Write a function `evaluate(batches)` accepting a list of tuples with bean origin, roast time in minutes, and maximum temperature. Use classes for a bean batch, a roast profile, and a quality controller. The roast profile considers a batch perfect if the roast time is between ten and fifteen minutes and temperature between two hundred and two hundred twenty. The bean batch holds the origin and data. The quality controller assesses each bean batch using the roast profile. Return a list of bean origins that meet the perfect criteria. Example: Colombia beans roasted for twelve minutes at two hundred ten degrees. Output: a list with Colombia.

title: Charity Campaign Tracker
spec: Write a function `track(donations)` processing a list of tuples containing donor name, donation amount, and whether it is recurring. Create classes for a campaign donor, a financial pledge, and a reward tier. The financial pledge stores the amount and recurring status, doubling the effective amount for recurring pledges. The campaign donor links to their pledges. The reward tier grants a gold status if the effective total is over five hundred, otherwise silver. Return a list of tuples with donor name and their reward tier status. Example: a recurring donation of three hundred. Output: a list with the name and gold.

title: Pizza Delivery Dispatch
spec: Write a function `dispatch(orders)` taking a list of tuples with customer name, distance in miles, and number of pizzas. Design classes for a hungry customer, a pizza order, and a delivery driver. The pizza order takes twenty minutes to prepare. The delivery driver travels at thirty miles per hour, so each mile takes two minutes. The hungry customer aggregates the total time from prep to arrival. The dispatch logic routes the delivery driver to calculate expected delivery times. Return a list of tuples with customer name and total minutes until arrival. Example: a customer five miles away ordering two pizzas. Output: a list with their name and thirty.

title: Library Due Date Manager
spec: Write a function `manage(loans)` processing a list of tuples with borrower name, book title, and days kept. Use classes for a library member, a borrowed book, and a fine calculator. The borrowed book allows a loan period of fourteen days. The fine calculator applies a penalty of two per day for each day kept beyond the loan period. The library member tracks the borrowed book and total fines owed. Determine the total fine for each library member. Return a list of tuples with borrower name and the calculated fine amount. Example: a member keeping a book for fifteen days. Output: a list with the member name and two.

title: Robot Vacuum Pathing
spec: Write a function `simulate(instructions)` that simulates a robot vacuum. The instructions are a list of string commands. You must model the cleaning environment using distinct entities for a floor tile, a dust bunny, and a charging station. The vacuum moves across the grid, picking up dirt when encountering a dust bunny and recharging when on a charging station. Each entity should track its own state, such as dirt level or charge available. Return a tuple of total dirt collected and final battery level. For example, moving over two dirt spots and a charger returns something like ten and one hundred.

title: Virtual Pet Simulator
spec: Write a function `simulate(events)` to manage a virtual pet environment. The events are a list of strings like feed or play. You must model different types of pets using distinct entities such as a fluffy dog, a scaly reptile, and a feathery bird, along with items like a food bowl and a chew toy. Each pet type has different rates of hunger and happiness reduction. Process each event by interacting with the appropriate entity to update its internal stats. Return a list of numbers representing the final happiness and hunger of each pet in the order they were created. For example, after two feeds and one play, the output might be a list of sevens and eights.

title: Music Synthesizer Engine
spec: Write a function `synthesize(notes)` that processes a sequence of note frequencies. To process these, model different audio components using distinct entities such as a sine oscillator, a square wave generator, and an envelope filter. Each component should take a frequency or audio level and apply its specific mathematical transformation. Route each note through an oscillator and then a filter, keeping a running total of the output amplitudes. Return the final summed amplitude as a rounded number. For instance, inputting three standard frequencies should yield a specific numeric total based on the component transformations.

title: Data Center Rack Management
spec: Write a function `allocate(workloads)` that assigns computing tasks to a server rack. The workloads are a list of numbers representing required processing power. Model the hardware using distinct entities such as a compute server, a storage array, and a network switch. Each hardware type has a maximum capacity and a power draw that increases as capacity is used. Distribute the workloads across the available hardware entities, turning on additional units only when the active ones reach capacity. Return a tuple containing the total power consumed and the number of active units. For example, given five small workloads, the output might be a power draw of four hundred and two active units.

title: Elevator Control System
spec: Write a function `dispatch(requests)` that processes building elevator calls. The requests are a list of tuples containing floor numbers and directions. Model the elevator system using distinct entities such as an elevator cabin, a floor button panel, and a door motor. Each entity should handle a part of the logic, like tracking current capacity, registering pressed buttons, and calculating the time to open and close doors. Calculate the total time taken to resolve all requests in the sequence. Return the total time in seconds as an integer. For example, picking up three people on different floors might take a total of forty five seconds.

title: Smart Greenhouse Controller
spec: Write a function `regulate(readings)` that adjusts greenhouse conditions. The readings are a list of tuples with temperature and moisture values. Model the environmental controls using distinct entities such as a vent fan, a heating mat, and a drip irrigator. Each control device should evaluate the current reading and determine if it needs to activate to restore the baseline climate, tracking how many minutes it runs. Iterate through the readings, applying the control devices to simulate the passage of time and resource usage. Return a list of total run times for each device type. For example, a sequence of cold and dry readings might return twenty minutes for heat and ten for water.

title: Drone Delivery Fleet
spec: Write a function `dispatch(deliveries)` to manage automated package drops. The deliveries are a list of package weights and distances. Model the delivery system using distinct entities such as a quad copter, a heavy lifter drone, and a charging pad. Each drone type has a different payload capacity, battery drain rate, and flight speed. Assign each delivery to the most efficient available drone, sending it to a charging pad if its battery falls too low. Return a tuple with the total flight time and the number of charge cycles used. A set of three light packages might result in forty minutes of flight and zero charges.

title: Vending Machine Dispenser
spec: Write a function `vend(selections)` that processes vending machine purchases. The selections are a list of inserted coin values and item codes. Model the machine using distinct entities such as a coin slot mechanism, a snack coil dispenser, and a return lever. The coin slot must tally the inserted money, the snack coil checks stock and triggers a drop, and the return lever calculates any necessary change. Process each transaction in order, keeping a tally of the machine's total revenue and the number of items sold. Return a tuple of the final revenue and total items dispensed. For example, three successful purchases might yield five dollars and three items.

title: Arcade Game Cabinet
spec: Write a function `play(tokens)` that simulates playing arcade games. The tokens is a list of token counts inserted into different machines. Model the arcade using distinct entities such as a claw machine, a coin pusher, and a pinball table. Each game has a different cost per play, a win probability, and a ticket payout rate. Deduct the tokens to play the games, simulating the outcomes based on their internal rules and accumulating the won tickets. Return the total number of tickets won across all games. For example, twenty tokens spent mostly on pinball might yield fifty tickets.

title: Cyber Security Scanner
spec: Write a function `scan(network)` that evaluates a network for vulnerabilities. The network is a list of strings representing different device endpoints. Model the scanning process using distinct entities such as a fire wall rule, a port scanner, and a threat signature database. Each entity should inspect the endpoints, looking for specific patterns like an open remote port or an outdated software version, and assign a threat score. Aggregate the threat scores for all endpoints to determine the overall risk level of the network. Return the total risk score as an integer. For instance, scanning three secure endpoints and one exposed endpoint might return a score of fifteen.

title: Mutual Fund Allocator
spec: Write a function `allocate(funds)` that distributes investment capital. The funds is a list of dollar amounts. Model the investment vehicles using distinct entities such as a growth stock, a treasury bond, and an index fund. Each investment type has a specific risk multiplier and an expected annual yield. Route the incoming funds into these entities based on a fixed percentage split, calculating the projected return for each over a year. Return a list of the projected dollar returns for each investment type. For example, investing one thousand dollars might yield fifty dollars in growth and twenty in bonds.

title: Telescope Observation Schedule
spec: Write a function `schedule(targets)` that plans astronomical observations. The targets are a list of sky coordinates and brightness levels. Model the observatory equipment using distinct entities such as a primary mirror, a tracking mount, and a digital sensor. Each piece of equipment requires different calibration times and exposure limits based on the brightness of the target. Calculate the total time required to calibrate and observe all the targets in sequence, adding cooldown periods if the tracking mount moves too far. Return the total observation time in minutes. Observing two bright stars and one faint galaxy might return one hundred and twenty minutes.

title: Brewery Fermentation Monitor
spec: Write a function `monitor(readings)` that tracks the brewing process. The readings are a list of tuples containing gravity and temperature. Model the brewing setup using distinct entities such as a fermentation tank, a cooling jacket, and a yeast culture. The yeast culture thrives at specific temperatures, the fermentation tank tracks the current gravity, and the cooling jacket turns on to lower the heat when necessary. Process the readings step by step to determine the final alcohol content and the number of times the cooling system activated. Return a tuple of the alcohol percentage and cooling cycles. A batch with high initial sugar might result in five percent alcohol and three cooling cycles.

title: Film Set Equipment Manager
spec: Write a function `setup(scenes)` that prepares equipment for movie shoots. The scenes are a list of lighting and camera requirements. Model the film gear using distinct entities such as a boom microphone, a cinema camera, and a lighting rig. Each piece of gear requires a specific setup time, a power draw, and a designated crew member to operate it. Iterate through the scenes, tallying the total setup time and the peak power draw required by the active equipment. Return a tuple of the maximum power draw and the total setup time in minutes. Setting up for two complex scenes might return two thousand watts and eighty minutes.

title: Block Chain Node Manager
spec: Write a function `mine(blocks)` that simulates block chain processing. The blocks are a list of difficulty integers. Model the network using distinct entities such as a validation node, a cryptographic hasher, and a peer network. The validation node checks the incoming block, the cryptographic hasher expends processing power to solve the difficulty, and the peer network broadcasts the result. Track the total processing power expended and the number of blocks successfully added to the chain. Return a tuple of total power used and blocks mined. Processing five blocks of varying difficulty might return one million hashes and five blocks.

title: Wind Farm Energy Simulator
spec: Write a function `simulate(winds)` that calculates power generation. The winds are a list of wind speeds in miles per hour. Model the wind farm using distinct entities such as a turbine blade, a rotary generator, and a battery bank. The turbine blade converts wind speed into mechanical spin, the rotary generator turns spin into electrical watts, and the battery bank stores the excess power up to its capacity. Process the sequence of wind speeds to calculate the total power generated and the final stored energy. Return a tuple of generated watts and stored watts. Ten hours of moderate wind might return five thousand watts generated and one thousand stored.

title: Water Purification Plant
spec: Write a function `purify(samples)` that processes contaminated water. The samples are a list of numbers representing contamination levels. Model the treatment stages using distinct entities such as a sediment filter, a chemical mixer, and an ultraviolet lamp. The water must pass through each stage, where the sediment filter removes large particles, the chemical mixer neutralizes toxins based on volume, and the ultraviolet lamp eliminates bacteria. Track the operating cost of each stage as the contamination is reduced to safe levels. Return the total operating cost as a number. Processing five highly contaminated samples might return an operating cost of fifty.

title: Cargo Train Manifest
spec: Write a function `load(crates)` that organizes a freight train. The crates are a list of weights and material types. Model the train using distinct entities such as a locomotive engine, a flatbed car, and a box car. The locomotive engine provides a maximum pulling force, while the flatbed cars and box cars have different weight limits and rules for what materials they can hold safely. Distribute the crates among the train cars, adding new cars to the train as needed until the locomotive reaches its pulling limit. Return the total number of cars used and the total weight loaded. Loading twenty heavy crates might result in five cars and ten thousand pounds.

title: Mars Rover Explorer
spec: Write a function `explore(commands)` that navigates a planetary rover. The commands are a list of directional movements and action strings. Model the rover's systems using distinct entities such as a wheel motor, a solar panel, and a soil drill. The wheel motor drains power to move, the solar panel recharges power during specific time intervals, and the soil drill consumes extra power to collect samples. Execute the commands in order, managing the shared power reserve so that the rover powers down if the battery hits zero. Return the number of successful movements and the number of samples collected. Ten commands might result in six movements and two samples.

title: Printing Press Operator
spec: Write a function `process(jobs)` that processes a queue of print requests. The jobs are a list of page counts and color types. Model the print shop using distinct entities such as a paper feeder, a cyan cartridge, and a drying heater. The paper feeder tracks paper jams, the cyan cartridge depletes ink based on color intensity, and the drying heater runs longer for full color pages. Process each job by deducting resources and calculating the time taken, stopping early if ink or paper runs out. Return a tuple of completed jobs and total time elapsed in seconds. Processing four color jobs might yield three completed jobs and three hundred seconds.

title: Deep Sea Submarine
spec: Write a function `dive(depths)` that monitors a submarine descent. The depths are a list of target depth changes in meters. Model the submarine using distinct entities such as a ballast tank, a pressure hull, and a sonar array. The ballast tank controls water intake to change depth, the pressure hull tracks structural stress based on the current depth, and the sonar array pings for obstacles. Update the state of each entity as the submarine moves to each target depth, recording the maximum structural stress encountered. Return the final depth and the maximum stress value. A dive sequence dropping five hundred meters might return a depth of five hundred and a stress of eighty.

title: Bank Vault Security
spec: Write a function `secure(events)` that processes security triggers in a bank. The events are a list of string codes representing sensor trips. Model the security system using distinct entities such as a motion detector, a seismic sensor, and an alarm siren. Each sensor type has a different sensitivity threshold and a time window before it resets. If multiple sensors are tripped within a short time, the alarm siren activates and logs the breach. Track the sequence of events to determine how many times the alarm sounded and which sensor was tripped most frequently. Return a tuple of the alarm count and the most active sensor string. Ten events might trigger two alarms and motion as the most active.

title: Textile Mill Loom
spec: Write a function `weave(patterns)` that simulates weaving fabrics. The patterns are a list of thread colors and lengths. Model the loom machinery using distinct entities such as a thread spool, a shuttle mechanism, and a tension spring. The thread spool dispenses yardage, the shuttle mechanism moves back and forth consuming power, and the tension spring adjusts based on the thread thickness to prevent snapping. Iterate through the patterns, simulating the fabric creation while tracking thread usage and mechanical wear on the tension spring. Return the total yards woven and the final mechanical wear percentage. Weaving five complex patterns might yield fifty yards and ten percent wear.

title: Satellite Communications Relay
spec: Write a function `transmit(signals)` that routes data through a satellite network. The signals are a list of data packet sizes. Model the network using distinct entities such as a ground station, a low orbit satellite, and a geostationary satellite. The ground station uploads the data, the low orbit satellite provides fast but intermittent connections, and the geostationary satellite offers continuous but slower throughput. Route each packet through the optimal path based on its size, calculating the transmission delay and dropping packets if a buffer overflows. Return a tuple of successful transmissions and average delay in milliseconds. Transmitting ten packets might return nine successes and two hundred milliseconds delay.

title: Amusement Park Ride Simulator
spec: Write a function `operate(riders)` that manages a theme park attraction. The riders are a list of group sizes. Model the ride using distinct entities such as a safety harness, a passenger cart, and a track brake. The passenger cart can only hold a maximum number of people, the safety harness must be engaged for each boarded passenger, and the track brake wears down slightly with every dispatched cart. Group the riders into the carts without splitting groups if possible, run the safety checks, and dispatch the carts. Return the total number of carts dispatched and the final brake wear percentage. Processing fifty riders in small groups might result in fifteen carts and five percent wear.

title: Cloud Resource Biller
spec: A system receives a list of cloud resources to provision, each given as a string. Define separate small classes for a compute instance, a storage volume, a database cluster, and a load balancer. Each class should have a method to return its hourly cost: fifty for compute, ten for storage, one hundred for database, and twenty five for balancer. Write an entry function `invoice(requests)` that takes the list of strings, instantiates the corresponding objects, and returns the total sum of their hourly costs. Ignore unknown strings. For example, given a list with two compute, one storage, and one balancer, it should return one hundred thirty five.

title: UI Component Renderer
spec: A layout engine processes a list of interface elements. Define separate classes for a text input, a radio button, a checkbox group, and a submit button. Each class should provide a method returning its vertical height in pixels: text is thirty, radio is twenty, checkbox is forty, and submit is fifty. Write an entry function `layout(components)` that takes a list of string identifiers and maps them to instances of these classes. The function should iterate through the instantiated objects and return their total vertical height. Unknown elements should be skipped. For example, a list with one text, one radio, and one submit should return one hundred.

title: Supply Chain Node Evaluator
spec: A logistics planner calculates transit delays across different facilities. Create individual classes for a manufacturing plant, a distribution center, a regional warehouse, and a retail store. Each class must have a method yielding its average processing delay in hours: seventy two for manufacturing, twenty four for distribution, twelve for warehouse, and four for retail. Write a function `evaluate(route)` that takes a list of strings representing the path of a product, creates the matching objects, and calculates the total delay hours. For example, a route from manufacturing to distribution to retail should result in one hundred hours.

title: Graphic Novel Panel Arranger
spec: A comic book design tool measures the total width of a page layout. Define distinct classes for a splash panel, a dialogue panel, a wide establishing panel, and a tall action panel. Each class should implement a method that returns its width in centimeters: splash is twenty, dialogue is five, wide is fifteen, and tall is ten.
