Write the function `arrange(panels)` that accepts a list of panel type strings, builds the corresponding objects, and returns the total width across the page. For example, one splash and two dialogues should return thirty.

title: Particle Physics Collider
spec: A simulation tracks subatomic particles in a collider. Create separate classes for an alpha particle, a beta particle, a gamma photon, and a neutrino beam. Each class needs a method to report its relative energy level: alpha is four, beta is one, gamma is ten, and neutrino is zero. Write an entry function `simulate(particles)` that processes a list of particle name strings by instantiating the appropriate objects, then computes and returns the total energy of the collision. Ignore any unrecognized strings. For example, a list with one alpha, two betas, and one gamma should return sixteen.

title: Payment Processor Router
spec: An online checkout system handles various payment methods. Define separate classes for a credit card, a bank transfer, a digital wallet, and a gift card. Each class must contain a method returning its flat transaction fee in cents: credit is thirty, bank is zero, wallet is fifteen, and gift is five. Write a function `process(methods)` that takes a list of payment type strings, creates the corresponding objects, and returns the total transaction fees collected. Unrecognized strings add nothing. For example, one credit, one wallet, and two gifts should return fifty five cents.

title: Chemical Reaction Yield
spec: A laboratory simulator calculates the energy output of various reactions. Define distinct classes for a synthesis reaction, a decomposition reaction, a displacement reaction, and a combustion reaction. Each class should have a method returning its exothermic energy value: synthesis is twenty, decomposition is negative ten, displacement is five, and combustion is fifty. Write a function `calculate(reactions)` that takes a list of reaction type strings, instantiates the matching objects, and sums their total energy output. Unmatched strings are ignored. For example, one combustion, one synthesis, and one decomposition should return sixty.

title: Marine Biology Sampler
spec: A research expedition script tallies sample collection times. Create individual classes for a coral fragment, a sediment core, a water vial, and a plankton net. Each class needs a method to report its collection time in minutes: coral is twenty, sediment is thirty, water is five, and plankton is fifteen. Write an entry function `sample(items)` that takes a list of item strings, instantiates the proper objects, and returns the sum of all their collection times. If an item string is unrecognized, it should be ignored. For example, two water vials and one coral fragment should return thirty.

title: Restaurant Menu Compiler
spec: A digital dining system calculates the preparation time for an order. Define small classes for a hot appetizer, a cold salad, a main entree, and a sweet dessert. Each class must have a method that returns its prep time in minutes: appetizer is ten, salad is five, entree is twenty five, and dessert is fifteen. Write a function `compile(items)` that processes a list of dish strings by building the corresponding objects and returns the total required prep time in minutes. Unrecognized strings are skipped. For example, one cold salad and one main entree should return thirty.

title: Online Course Builder
spec: An e-learning platform calculates the total runtime of a course module. Create separate classes for a video lesson, an audio podcast, an interactive quiz, and a reading assignment. Each class should provide a method returning its estimated completion time in minutes: video is twenty, audio is fifteen, quiz is ten, and reading is thirty. Write the function `build(modules)` that takes a list of module strings, creates instances of these classes, and computes the total duration of the course. For example, one video, one quiz, and one reading should return sixty minutes.

title: Martial Arts Tournament Bracket
spec: A sporting event script computes the duration of different match types. Define separate classes for a sparring match, a board breaking event, a weapons demonstration, and a grappling bout. Each class should have a method returning its allocated time in minutes: sparring is ten, breaking is five, weapons is fifteen, and grappling is twenty. Write an entry function `schedule(events)` that takes a list of event strings, instantiates the appropriate objects, and returns the total tournament duration. Unmatched events are ignored. For example, one sparring and one breaking should return fifteen.

title: Concert Merchandise Stand
spec: A tour management script calculates revenue from swag sales. Create small classes for a graphic tshirt, a tour poster, a vinyl record, and a cotton hoodie. Each class needs a method to return the price: tshirt is thirty, poster is fifteen, record is forty, and hoodie is sixty. Write a function `sell(items)` that reads a list of item strings, instantiates the corresponding objects, and returns the total merchandise revenue. Ignore unknown items. For example, two posters and one tshirt should return sixty.

title: Forensic Evidence Processor
spec: A crime lab script tracks the processing time for gathered evidence. Define classes for a fingerprint slide, a dna swab, a ballistic casing, and a fabric fiber. Each class should have a method returning its analysis time in hours: fingerprint is two, dna is forty eight, ballistic is four, and fabric is twelve. Write a function `process(evidence)` that takes a list of evidence strings, builds the matching objects, and calculates the total hours needed for analysis. Unknown evidence adds nothing. For example, one fingerprint and one ballistic should return six.

title: Office Floorplan Evaluator
spec: An architectural tool estimates the capacity of a commercial office building. Create distinct classes for a conference room, a break room, a private office, and an open workspace. Each class must provide a method to return its maximum occupancy: conference is twenty, break is fifteen, private is two, and workspace is forty. Write a function `plan(rooms)` that accepts a list of room strings, instantiates the proper objects, and returns the total occupancy of the building. Unrecognized strings are skipped. For example, one conference room and two private offices should return twenty four.

title: Tax Deduction Analyzer
spec: A financial software calculates total allowable deductions. Define separate classes for a medical expense, an educational expense, a charitable donation, and a business expense. Each class should have a method that applies a specific deduction limit: medical returns up to five hundred, educational returns up to two hundred, charitable returns up to one thousand, and business returns up to three hundred. Write a function `analyze(expenses)` that takes a list of expense type strings, creates the corresponding objects, and returns the maximum potential deduction by summing their limits. For example, one medical and one charitable should return one thousand five hundred.

title: Software Testing Framework
spec: A continuous integration tool aggregates test outcomes. Create separate classes for a passed test, a failed test, a skipped test, and an errored test. Each class must have a method returning its severity score: passed is zero, failed is ten, skipped is one, and errored is twenty. Write an entry function `evaluate(results)` that takes a list of result strings, instantiates the corresponding objects, and returns the total severity score of the test suite. Unknown outcomes are ignored. For example, two passed, one failed, and one skipped should return eleven.

title: Historical Artifact Appraiser
spec: A museum script estimates the insurance value of a new exhibit. Define separate classes for a clay pottery piece, a bronze weapon, a gold coin, and a marble bust. Each class should provide a method returning its base appraisal value in thousands: pottery is five, weapon is twenty, coin is fifty, and bust is one hundred. Write a function `appraise(artifacts)` that reads a list of artifact strings, creates instances of these classes, and computes the total appraisal value. Unmatched artifacts add zero. For example, one pottery piece and two gold coins should return one hundred five.

title: Dental Clinic Biller
spec: A healthcare script calculates the total cost of a patient visit. Create individual classes for a routine cleaning, a cavity filling, a root canal, and a crown placement. Each class needs a method to report its service cost: cleaning is one hundred, filling is two hundred, canal is eight hundred, and crown is one thousand. Write a function `bill(services)` that takes a list of service strings, builds the matching objects, and calculates the total cost. Unrecognized strings are ignored. For example, one cleaning and two fillings should return five hundred.

title: Hardware Store Inventory
spec: A retail script weighs bulk items for shipping. Define classes for a steel hammer, a power drill, a tape measure, and a socket wrench. Each class must have a method returning its weight in ounces: hammer is twenty four, drill is sixty, tape is ten, and wrench is sixteen. Write a function `weigh(tools)` that accepts a list of tool strings, instantiates the proper objects, and computes the total shipping weight. Unrecognized strings are skipped. For example, two hammers and one tape should return fifty eight.

title: Magic Show Prop Organizer
spec: A theater production script calculates the cubic volume of stage equipment. Create separate classes for a trap door, a velvet curtain, a smoke machine, and a trick box. Each class should provide a method yielding its volume in cubic feet: trap is ten, curtain is five, smoke is two, and trick is fifteen. Write an entry function `organize(props)` that takes a list of prop strings, instantiates the corresponding objects, and returns the total cubic volume required in the storage truck. Unmatched props are ignored. For example, one smoke machine and one trick box should return seventeen.

title: Social Media Feed Aggregator
spec: A content platform calculates the engagement score of a user timeline. Define individual classes for a text post, an image post, a video post, and a link share. Each class needs a method returning its base engagement multiplier: text is one, image is three, video is five, and link is two. Write a function `aggregate(posts)` that processes a list of post type strings by instantiating the matching objects and summing their multipliers. Ignore any unknown strings. For example, two text posts and one video post should return seven.

title: Smart City Sensor Network
spec: An urban management system polls remote environmental monitors. Create distinct classes for a pollution monitor, a traffic camera, a noise sensor, and a weather station. Each class must have a method that returns its data payload size in kilobytes: pollution is twelve, traffic is two hundred, noise is eight, and weather is fifteen. Write a function `poll(sensors)` that reads a list of sensor strings, builds the matching objects, and calculates the total data bandwidth required. For example, one traffic camera and two noise sensors should return two hundred sixteen.

title: Optical Lens Array
spec: A camera engineering tool calculates light transmission loss. Define separate classes for a convex lens, a concave lens, a polarizing filter, and a glass prism. Each class should implement a method returning its light loss percentage: convex is two, concave is three, polarizing is fifty, and prism is ten. Write an entry function `focus(components)` that takes a list of component strings, instantiates the appropriate objects, and computes the total light loss percentage by summing them. Unrecognized strings are skipped. For example, one convex and one polarizing should return fifty two.

title: Warehouse Conveyor Belt
spec: A distribution center script times sorting operations. Create distinct classes for a barcode scanner, a weighing scale, a diverter arm, and a wrapping machine. Each class must provide a method returning its processing time in seconds: scanner is two, scale is five, diverter is three, and wrapping is fifteen. Write a function `sort(stages)` that takes a list of stage strings, creates instances of these classes, and returns the total sorting time. Ignore unknown stages. For example, one scanner and one diverter should return five.

title: Television Broadcast Scheduler
spec: A media script calculates the runtime of a programming block. Define small classes for a news bulletin, a sitcom episode, a documentary feature, and a commercial break. Each class needs a method to report its airtime in minutes: news is thirty, sitcom is twenty, documentary is sixty, and commercial is five. Write a function `schedule(programs)` that reads a list of program strings, instantiates the corresponding objects, and returns the total broadcast minutes. For example, one sitcom and two commercials should return thirty.

title: Inbox Spam Filter
spec: Write a function `filter(messages)` that processes a list of email tuples containing a sender email, a subject string, a body string, and an attachment count. Design an object oriented solution where four distinct filtering rules are represented by separate types. Define a rule for matching banned sender domains, a rule for forbidden phrases in the subject, a rule for a maximum body length, and a rule for a maximum attachment count. Instantiate one of each rule type with sample criteria, such as banning the domain spammer dot com, forbidding the phrase buy now, limiting the body to two hundred characters, and limiting attachments to zero. Evaluate each message against all four rule objects. Return a list of subjects of the messages that pass every rule. For example, given a message from good at email dot com with subject hello, body world, and zero attachments, it passes all rules and its subject is returned in the list.

title: Bot Response Formatter
spec: Implement `respond(intents)` which takes a list of user intent strings and translates them into chatbot actions. Define four distinct object types representing actions: a plain text reply, an image attachment, a clickable button menu, and a typing delay. For a greeting intent, produce a typing delay of one second and a text reply of hello. For a product intent, produce an image attachment of the product and a button menu with buy and cancel options. For a goodbye intent, produce a delay of two seconds and a text reply of farewell. Iterate over the input intents, instantiate the appropriate action objects, and collect them in a list. Then call a render method on each action object in the list. Return a list of strings where each string is the rendered description of that action. For example, an input of greeting and goodbye results in a list containing delay one second, reply hello, delay two seconds, and reply farewell.

title: Input Field Validator
spec: Create a function `validate(inputs)` that checks a list of user inputs. Define four separate object types to represent validation constraints: a minimum length constraint, a maximum length constraint, an allowed characters constraint, and a forbidden prefix constraint. Instantiate these four constraint types to require a minimum length of eight, a maximum length of twenty, only alphanumeric characters, and forbidding the prefix admin. The function should iterate over the list of input strings and evaluate each one against all four constraint objects. Return a list of strings containing only the inputs that satisfy every constraint. For example, the input user one two three passes all criteria, while the input admin user passes length but fails the forbidden prefix constraint.

title: Questionnaire Scorer
spec: Write `score(answers)` to process a list of answers for a survey. Model the survey questions using four distinct object types: a multiple choice question, a true false question, a numeric rating question, and a free text question. Instantiate one multiple choice question with the correct answer blue, one true false question with the correct answer true, one numeric rating question requiring a value of five, and one free text question that simply requires a non empty response. The input is a list of answer sets, where each set is a tuple of four responses corresponding to the four questions. For each answer set, use the question objects to evaluate the responses. Award one point for each correct or valid response. Return a list of total integer scores for each answer set. For example, an answer set of blue, true, five, and good job scores four points.

title: Storage Directory Tree
spec: Provide a function `measure(nodes)` that computes the total size of different file system items. Design an object oriented system defining four types of file system items: a regular file, a compressed archive, a symbolic link, and a directory folder. A regular file has a direct size. A compressed archive has a size that is half of its original uncompressed size. A symbolic link always has a size of zero. A directory folder has a size equal to the sum of its contents plus a four kilobyte overhead. The input is a list of tuples detailing the item kind and its associated size or contents. Based on the input, instantiate the appropriate item objects to build a flat list of these elements. Iterate through the objects and call a size calculation method on each. Return the total computed size of all items combined. For example, a regular file of ten kilobytes and a compressed archive of twenty kilobytes yields a total of twenty kilobytes.

title: Formula Tree Evaluator
spec: Implement `evaluate(instructions)` to calculate the result of mathematical operations. Define four distinct types of expression nodes: a constant value node, an addition operation node, a multiplication operation node, and a maximum value operation node. Each operation node type should take other nodes as its inputs. The function receives a list of instruction tuples representing a tree of operations. Translate the instructions by instantiating the appropriate node objects to build the mathematical tree. For example, a constant node simply returns its value, while an addition node returns the sum of its two child nodes. Once the entire tree of node objects is constructed from the input, call an evaluation method on the root node. Return the final computed integer result. For example, an addition node combining a constant five and a constant ten evaluates to fifteen.

title: Window Widget Layout
spec: Write a function `arrange(widgets)` that calculates the total width required by a series of graphical interface elements. Create four separate types to represent widget elements: a text label, a push button, a horizontal spacer, and an image icon. A text label requires ten pixels per character. A push button requires ten pixels per character plus a twenty pixel border. A horizontal spacer takes a fixed width provided at creation. An image icon requires a fixed width of fifty pixels. The input is a list of tuples containing the widget type and an associated value like text content or spacer width. Instantiate the correct object for each widget based on the input tuples. Iterate through the created objects and sum their calculated widths. Return the total integer width required for the entire layout. For example, an image icon and a horizontal spacer of width twenty require a total of seventy pixels.

title: Wealth Asset Tracker
spec: Create `appraise(portfolio)` to calculate the total value of different financial holdings. Use an object oriented design with four distinct types of assets: a cash account, a stock holding, a real estate property, and a government bond. A cash account simply returns its balance. A stock holding returns its share count multiplied by its current price. A real estate property returns its original value increased by a fixed appreciation percentage. A government bond returns its principal plus accrued fixed interest. The input is a list of tuples describing the asset types and their relevant numbers. Iterate over the input, instantiate the corresponding asset objects, and gather them into a list. Loop through the list of asset objects to compute their individual current values. Return the total aggregated value of the portfolio. For example, a cash account with one thousand and a government bond with a principal of five hundred and interest of fifty yields a total of one thousand five hundred and fifty.

title: Cooking Instruction Parser
spec: Implement a function `parse(recipe)` that translates a list of cooking steps into time estimates. Define four types of recipe steps as distinct objects: a preparation step, a resting step, a stovetop boiling step, and an oven baking step. A preparation step takes a fixed five minutes per ingredient. A resting step takes exactly the specified rest time. A stovetop boiling step takes ten minutes to heat up plus the specified boiling time. An oven baking step takes fifteen minutes to preheat plus the specified baking duration. The input is a list of tuples describing the step kind and its associated quantity or duration. Instantiate the appropriate step objects based on the input and collect them into a sequence. Call a time estimation method on each step object and return the total integer minutes required for the recipe. For example, a resting step of twenty minutes followed by a stovetop boiling step of five minutes requires thirty five minutes total.

title: Markdown Parser Engine
spec: Write `convert(lines)` to process a list of raw text lines into basic hypertext format. Design the system using four distinct object types for text blocks: a normal paragraph, a primary header, a bullet list item, and a block quote. A normal paragraph wraps text in standard paragraph tags. A primary header wraps text in heading one tags. A bullet list item wraps text in list item tags. A block quote wraps text in blockquote tags. The input list contains tuples of a block type identifier and the text content. Iterate over the input tuples and instantiate the corresponding block objects. Then, iterate over the objects and call a formatting method on each. Return a single joined string of the formatted hypertext output. For example, a primary header with text welcome becomes heading one tags wrapping the word welcome.

title: Task Trigger Engine
spec: Implement a function `check(conditions)` that determines if a scheduled background job should run. Define four distinct object types representing trigger conditions: a time of day trigger, a day of week trigger, a file presence trigger, and a memory threshold trigger. The time of day trigger passes if the current hour matches its target. The day of week trigger passes if the current day matches. The file presence trigger passes if a specified file name is in a list of existing files. The memory threshold trigger passes if the available memory is above a certain amount. Instantiate one of each trigger type using predefined target values. The input provides the current hour, current day, existing files, and available memory. Evaluate the four trigger objects using the input data. Return the boolean true if all triggers pass, otherwise false. For example, if all target thresholds and schedules match the current state provided in the input, the function returns true.

title: Sound Wave Processor
spec: Create `process(audio)` to simulate applying sound effects to an initial audio signal represented by an integer. Define four separate types for audio effects: a volume boost effect, a signal delay effect, a distortion effect, and a noise reduction effect. The volume boost multiplies the signal by a given factor. The signal delay subtracts a given amount from the signal. The distortion effect caps the signal at a maximum threshold. The noise reduction effect sets the signal to zero if it falls below a minimum threshold. The input is a starting integer signal and a list of effect tuples indicating the effect kind and its parameter. For each tuple, instantiate the proper effect object. Apply each effect object in sequence to the audio signal. Return the final modified integer signal. For example, an initial signal of ten with a volume boost of two and a signal delay of five results in fifteen.

title: Source Code Lexer
spec: Write `tokenize(code)` to classify words in a string of programming code. Design four distinct types of code tokens: a language keyword token, a numeric literal token, a string literal token, and an identifier token. A keyword token represents reserved words like if and return. A numeric literal token represents numbers. A string literal token represents text enclosed in quotes. An identifier token represents variable names. The input is a list of space separated words. Iterate over the words, determine the category of each word, and instantiate the corresponding token object. The token objects should have a method that returns a descriptive string of their classification and value. Return a list of these descriptive strings for all words in the input. For example, parsing the word if produces a string like language keyword token if.

title: Unit Test Runner
spec: Implement `run(assertions)` to evaluate the results of software tests. Model test conditions using four distinct object types: an equality assertion, a boolean true assertion, a boolean false assertion, and a null value assertion. The equality assertion takes an expected value and an actual value and passes if they match. The boolean true assertion passes if its value is true. The boolean false assertion passes if its value is false. The null value assertion passes if its value is exactly none. The input is a list of tuples containing the assertion kind and the value or values to check. Instantiate the appropriate assertion objects based on the input. Call an evaluation method on each object to determine if it passes. Return a count of how many assertions successfully passed. For example, an equality assertion comparing five and five and a boolean true assertion checking true will return a count of two passing tests.

title: Server Log Filter
spec: Create a function `sift(logs)` that extracts important information from server event records. Define four distinct filtering criteria as objects: a severity level filter, a date range filter, a specific module filter, and an error code filter. The severity filter passes events matching a given severity like critical. The date range filter passes events within a starting and ending day. The module filter passes events from a given system module. The error code filter passes events containing a specific numeric code. Instantiate these four filter objects with criteria targeting critical errors from the database module between day one and day ten with error code five hundred. The input is a list of log event tuples. Evaluate each event against the four filter objects. Return a list of the original strings of the events that pass all filters. For example, a critical error from the database module on day five with code five hundred is included in the final list.

title: Battle Action Resolver
spec: Write `resolve(turns)` to calculate the outcome of a combat sequence in a game. Define four distinct object types for character actions: a physical strike action, a magical spell action, a defensive block action, and a healing potion action. A physical strike reduces the opponent health by its damage value minus the opponent armor. A magical spell reduces health by its full damage value ignoring armor. A defensive block adds to the user armor for the turn. A healing potion increases the user health by a fixed amount. The input is a list of tuples detailing the action type and its power value. Start with two characters having one hundred health and zero armor. Instantiate the correct action objects from the input and apply their effects in order to the characters. Return a tuple containing the final health of both characters. For example, a physical strike of twenty against zero armor followed by a healing potion of ten leaves the target with ninety health.

title: Package Delivery Router
spec: Implement a function `route(packages)` to calculate the delivery cost for different shipping methods. Design an object oriented solution with four distinct types of delivery services: a standard ground delivery, an overnight air express, a refrigerated transport, and an oversized freight transport. Standard ground costs two dollars per pound. Overnight air costs five dollars per pound plus a ten dollar fee. Refrigerated transport costs three dollars per pound plus a twenty dollar cooling fee. Oversized freight costs a flat rate of fifty dollars plus one dollar per pound. The input is a list of tuples containing the delivery type and the package weight. Instantiate the respective delivery objects based on the input tuples. Iterate through the objects to calculate the shipping cost for each. Return the total sum of all delivery costs. For example, standard delivery for a ten pound package costs twenty dollars, and overnight air for the same weight costs sixty dollars.

title: Web Form Builder
spec: Create `render(fields)` to generate HTML snippets for user input forms. Define four distinct types of form elements as objects: a single line text input, a masked password input, a multi line text area, and a drop down selection. A single line text input produces an input tag with type text. A masked password input produces an input tag with type password. A multi line text area produces a textarea tag. A drop down selection produces a select tag containing option tags for its choices. The input is a list of tuples specifying the element type, its name, and an optional list of choices. Instantiate the appropriate element objects for each item in the input. Call a rendering method on each object to generate its markup. Return a single string containing all the joined HTML snippets. For example, a single line text input produces an input tag which is appended to the final string.

title: Customer Subscription Biller
spec: Write a function `bill(customers)` that calculates the monthly charges for software users. Use an object oriented approach to define four subscription plan types: a free tier plan, a basic monthly plan, a premium annual plan, and an enterprise seat plan. The free tier plan always charges zero. The basic monthly plan charges fifteen dollars. The premium annual plan charges one hundred and twenty dollars divided by twelve for the monthly rate. The enterprise seat plan charges ten dollars multiplied by the number of active users. The input is a list of tuples describing the plan type and the number of users if applicable. For each customer, instantiate the corresponding plan object. Iterate over these plan objects and call a billing method on each to determine the monthly charge. Return the total revenue calculated for the month. For example, two basic monthly plans and one free tier plan generate thirty dollars of revenue.

title: Network Path Finder
spec: Implement `search(network)` to simulate traversing nodes in a computer network. Define four distinct object types for network components: a regular workstation node, a routing switch node, a hardware firewall node, and a database server node. A workstation node takes one millisecond to process a request. A routing switch node takes two milliseconds. A hardware firewall node takes five milliseconds due to security checks. A database server node takes ten milliseconds to retrieve records. The input is a list of strings representing the sequence of components a request passes through. Map each string to the appropriate node object and instantiate them, forming a path list. Loop through the path list and invoke a processing method on each node to accumulate the latency. Return the total latency in milliseconds for the entire path. For example, a path of a regular workstation and a routing switch has a total latency of three milliseconds.

title: Street Intersection Phasing
spec: Create a function `simulate(traffic)` that models the timing of traffic signals. Define four distinct object types to represent signal phases: a primary green phase, a primary yellow phase, a pedestrian crossing phase, and an all red clearance phase. The primary green phase lasts for thirty seconds. The primary yellow phase lasts for four seconds. The pedestrian crossing phase lasts for twenty seconds. The all red clearance phase lasts for two seconds. The input is a list of phase identifiers that should be activated in sequence. Instantiate the correct phase objects based on the input identifiers and store them in a schedule list. Iterate through the schedule list and call a duration method on each phase object to calculate the total cycle time. Return the total cycle time in seconds. For example, a primary green phase followed by a primary yellow phase takes thirty four seconds.

title: Meeting Schedule Planner
spec: Write `schedule(events)` to allocate time for different types of corporate calendar appointments. Design an object oriented model with four event types: a daily standup meeting, a client presentation, a technical brainstorming session, and a quarterly review. A daily standup requires fifteen minutes. A client presentation requires sixty minutes plus thirty minutes of preparation. A technical brainstorming session requires forty five minutes. A quarterly review requires one hundred and twenty minutes. The input is a list of event type names requested for a given day. Instantiate the matching event objects for each requested item and add them to a daily itinerary list. Iterate over the itinerary list, calling a time requirement method on each object to accumulate the total minutes used. Return the total scheduled minutes. For example, a daily standup and a technical brainstorming session require sixty minutes total.

title: Neural Network Forward
spec: Implement a function `propagate(layers)` to calculate the output dimensions of a machine learning model. Model the network architecture using four distinct layer types: a fully connected dense layer, a two dimensional convolutional layer, a max pooling layer, and a flattening layer. A dense layer outputs a vector of a specific given size. A convolutional layer reduces the spatial dimensions of its input by two. A max pooling layer halves the spatial dimensions of its input. A flattening layer converts spatial dimensions into a single vector dimension by multiplying them. The input is an initial dimension tuple and a list of layer configurations. Instantiate the appropriate layer objects based on the configurations. Pass the initial dimensions through each layer object in sequence to compute the final output shape. Return the final dimension tuple. For example, an input dimension tuple of sixteen and sixteen passed through a max pooling layer results in a tuple of eight and eight.

title: SQL Query Builder
spec: Create `build(components)` to construct a database query string from logical parts. Define four distinct object types for query clauses: a select field clause, a from table clause, a where condition clause, and an order by clause. The select clause joins field names with commas. The from clause prefixes the table name with the word from. The where clause joins conditions with the word and. The order by clause appends the sort direction to the column name. The input is a list of tuples containing the clause type and its associated strings. Instantiate the corresponding clause objects for each tuple and store them in a list. Iterate through the list of clause objects and call a generation method on each to produce its SQL fragment. Return the final query string assembled by joining the fragments with spaces. For example, a select clause of id and name produces the string select id, name.

title: Repository Commit Log
spec: Write a function `format(commits)` to generate a readable history of source code changes. Design four distinct types of commit objects: a feature addition commit, a bug fix commit, a documentation update commit, and a version release commit. A feature addition prefixes its message with a star symbol. A bug fix prefixes its message with a plus symbol. A documentation update prefixes its message with a book word. A version release converts its message to all uppercase. The input is a list of tuples detailing the commit kind and its message text. Translate the input into a sequence of commit objects by instantiating the proper types. Iterate over the sequence and invoke a display method on each commit object to get the formatted message. Return a list of all formatted commit messages. For example, a bug fix commit with message fixed login outputs the string plus fixed login.

title: Ice Cream Sundae Builder
spec: Write a function `scoop(ingredients)` that calculates the total calories of a custom ice cream sundae. The input is a list of strings containing an ingredient type and its quantity separated by a space. Map each item to a separate dessert component object. A vanilla ingredient has two hundred calories per unit. A syrup ingredient has one hundred fifty calories per unit. A sprinkles ingredient has twenty calories per unit. A cherry ingredient has ten calories per unit. Sum the calories across all created component objects and return the integer total. Example: the input ["vanilla 2", "cherry 1"] yields a total of four hundred ten calories.

title: Chess Action Energy
spec: Write a function `validate(moves)` that estimates the energy cost of a sequence of chess maneuvers. The input is a list of strings where each string starts with an action type followed by a space and its target. For each string, create an object representing that specific maneuver to calculate its energy. A pawn move costs one energy point. A knight jump costs three energy points. A castle action costs five energy points. An enpassant capture costs four energy points. If an unrecognized action is encountered, it costs zero energy points. Sum the energy costs of all actions and return the total integer value. Example: the input ["pawn e4", "knight f3"] yields four.

title: Waste Recycling Sorter
spec: Write a function `sort(items)` that calculates the total recycling value in cents for a batch of waste items. The input is a list of strings containing an item material and its description separated by a space. Parse the strings and instantiate a dedicated handler for each material. A glass item is worth five cents. A cardboard item is worth two cents. A plastic item is worth three cents, but if its description includes the word bottle, it is worth six cents. An aluminum item is worth ten cents. Unrecognized materials are discarded with a value of zero. Return the total integer value in cents. Example: the list ["glass green", "plastic bottle"] yields eleven.

title: Photography Settings Exposure
spec: Write a function `expose(settings)` that calculates an exposure score based on camera configuration strings. The input is a list of strings, each denoting a setting name and its numeric or text value. Route each setting to its own representative object. For an aperture setting, the score is one hundred divided by the numeric value. For a shutter speed setting, the score is the numeric value divided by ten. For an iso level, the score is the numeric value divided by one hundred. For a white balance setting, the score is a flat five if the value is cloudy, or ten for any other value. Combine all the individual scores and return the total as a floating point number. Example: the input ["iso 400", "shutter 250"] returns twenty nine point zero.

title: Podcast Audio Clips
spec: Write a function `assemble(clips)` that determines the total compiled length in seconds of a podcast episode. The input is a list of strings describing the segment type and its raw duration in seconds. Instantiate a distinct timeline element for each type. An intro segment adds its raw duration plus five seconds of fade in. An interview clip adds its raw duration plus ten seconds of crossfade. A sponsor read adds exactly its raw duration. An outro segment adds its raw duration plus a trailing silence of eight seconds. Return the total integer duration. Example: the list ["intro 10", "sponsor 30"] results in forty five.

title: Gemstone Cutter Appraisal
spec: Write a function `appraise(gems)` that estimates the total retail value in dollars for a parcel of cut gemstones. The input is a list of strings providing the cut style and the carat weight. Map each string to a specific cut evaluator object. A round cut is valued at five thousand times the carat weight. A princess cut is valued at four thousand times the carat weight, plus a flat two hundred bonus. An emerald cut is valued at three thousand five hundred times the carat weight, minus a one hundred dollar polishing fee. A cushion cut is valued at three thousand times the carat weight. Sum and return the total float value. Example: the input ["round 2.0", "cushion 1.0"] yields thirteen thousand point zero.

title: Mountain Climbing Gear
spec: Write a function `pack(equipment)` that calculates the total weight in grams of a climbing bag. The input is a list of strings, each containing an equipment type and its quantity or length. Create specific gear models for each item to compute its weight. A rope weighs sixty grams per unit of length. A carabiner weighs eighty grams per quantity. A harness weighs four hundred grams per quantity. A piton weighs one hundred twenty grams per quantity. Ignore any unrecognized equipment. Return the integer total weight. Example: the input ["carabiner 2", "harness 1"] evaluates to five hundred sixty.

title: Olympic Gymnastics Routines
spec: Write a function `score(routines)` that computes the final all around score for a gymnast. The input is a list of strings containing an apparatus name and a base score. Use distinct objects to apply apparatus specific deductions or bonuses to the base score. A vault routine receives a bonus of zero point five. An uneven bars routine receives a penalty of zero point two. A balance beam routine has a deduction of zero point one. A floor exercise receives a bonus of zero point three. Sum all the modified scores and return a floating point number rounded to one decimal place. Example: the input ["vault 15.0", "beam 14.1"] results in twenty nine point five.

title: Laundry Machine Cycles
spec: Write a function `wash(cycles)` that calculates the total water usage in liters for a custom laundry program. The input is a list of strings indicating the cycle phase and its duration in minutes. Parse the phases and route them to their respective objects. A wash cycle uses two liters per minute. A rinse cycle uses three liters per minute. A spin cycle uses zero point five liters per minute. A drain cycle uses exactly zero liters, regardless of duration. Sum the water usage across all phases and return the float total. Example: the list ["wash 10", "spin 4"] outputs twenty two point zero.

title: Construction Materials Footprint
spec: Write a function `build(materials)` that calculates the carbon footprint in kilograms for a construction project. The input is a list of strings containing the material name and its quantity. Instantiate a specialized calculator for each material. A brick adds zero point five kilograms per unit. Concrete adds two hundred kilograms per unit. Timber subtracts ten kilograms per unit due to carbon sequestration. Steel adds five hundred kilograms per unit. Return the total float footprint. Example: the input ["concrete 2", "timber 10"] yields three hundred point zero.

title: Watch Complications Assembly
spec: Write a function `construct(features)` that estimates the assembly time in hours for a mechanical watch. The input is a list of strings, each giving a complication name and a complexity multiplier. Represent each feature with its own structural object. A chronograph takes twelve hours multiplied by the complexity. A moonphase takes eight hours multiplied by the complexity. A calendar takes fifteen hours multiplied by the complexity. A tourbillon takes fifty hours multiplied by the complexity. Add a base assembly time of twenty hours to the sum of the feature times, and return the integer total. Example: the input ["moonphase 2", "tourbillon 1"] yields eighty six.

title: Perfume Notes Evaporation
spec: Write a function `blend(notes)` that calculates the evaporation time in minutes of a custom fragrance. The input is a list of strings specifying the note tier and its volume in milliliters. Create distinct formula components for each tier. A top note evaporates at a rate of ten minutes per milliliter. A heart note lasts for forty minutes per milliliter. A base note persists for one hundred twenty minutes per milliliter. A fixative agent adds a flat two hundred minutes to the overall blend, regardless of its volume. Sum these times and return the total integer minutes. Example: the input ["top 2", "fixative 1"] results in two hundred twenty.

title: Fireworks Display Powder
spec: Write a function `ignite(shells)` that determines the total amount of black powder in grams needed for a pyrotechnic show. The input is a list of strings pairing a firework type with its quantity. Route each item to a specific class to compute its powder load. A rocket requires fifteen grams per unit. A fountain requires forty grams per unit. A roman requires ten grams per unit. An aerial requires one hundred fifty grams per unit. Combine the powder weights of all valid items and return the integer sum. Example: the input ["fountain 1", "aerial 2"] gives three hundred forty.

title: Microphone Components Cost
spec: Write a function `record(parts)` that calculates the manufacturing cost in dollars for custom studio microphones. The input is a list of strings indicating a part type and its quantity. Map each part to a specialized component object. A capsule costs fifty dollars per unit. A body costs twenty dollars per unit. A grille costs five dollars per unit. A connector costs ten dollars per unit. Accumulate the costs of all components in the list and return the integer total. Example: the input ["capsule 2", "grille 2"] evaluates to one hundred ten.

title: Wine Tasting Scoring
spec: Write a function `taste(notes)` that scores a wine out of one hundred points based on tasting observations. The input is a list of strings with the observation category and a descriptor. Instantiate separate reviewers for each category. A visual observation scores five points if the descriptor is clear, otherwise three points. An aroma observation scores fifteen points if the descriptor is fruity, otherwise ten. A palate observation scores forty points if it is dry, otherwise twenty. A finish observation scores twenty points if it is long, otherwise ten. Add a base score of ten to the sum of the reviewer scores and return the integer total. Example: the input ["visual clear", "aroma earthy"] produces twenty eight.

title: Guitar Pedals Latency
spec: Write a function `modulate(effects)` that calculates the latency in milliseconds introduced by a chain of audio effects. The input is a list of strings describing the effect pedal and its primary parameter value. Process the chain by creating a specific audio node for each effect. A distortion pedal adds a flat latency of two milliseconds. A delay pedal adds latency equal to its parameter value divided by ten. A reverb pedal adds latency equal to its parameter value divided by five. A chorus pedal adds a flat latency of fifteen milliseconds. Accumulate the latency for all pedals and return the float total. Example: the list ["distortion 5", "delay 200"] yields twenty two point zero.

title: Soil Layers Excavation
spec: Write a function `dig(layers)` that calculates the excavation cost in dollars for a landscaping project. The input is a list of strings, each giving a soil layer name and its depth in centimeters. Model each layer with a separate class to determine its cost. Humus costs one dollar per centimeter. Topsoil costs two dollars per centimeter. Subsoil costs five dollars per centimeter. Bedrock costs fifty dollars per centimeter. Multiply the depth by the corresponding rate for each layer, sum the results, and return the integer cost. Example: the input ["humus 10", "bedrock 2"] results in one hundred ten.

title: Origami Folds Complexity
spec: Write a function `fold(instructions)` that computes the complexity rating of an origami design. The input is a list of strings pairing a fold type with the number of times it is performed. Represent each operation with a unique fold class. A mountain fold adds one complexity point per action. A valley fold adds one complexity point per action. A squash fold adds three complexity points per action. A petal fold adds five complexity points per action. Accumulate the complexity points across all instructions and return the integer sum. Example: the list ["valley 2", "squash 1"] computes to five.

title: Juggling Props Appeal
spec: Write a function `toss(props)` that determines the crowd appeal score of a juggling act. The input is a list of strings containing a prop name and the quantity being juggled. Use dedicated evaluator objects for each prop type. A beanbag yields two appeal points per item. A club yields five appeal points per item. A ring yields four appeal points per item. A torch yields twenty appeal points per item. Multiply the quantity by the prop score, sum the results from the entire list, and return the integer appeal score. Example: the input ["beanbag 3", "torch 1"] yields twenty six.

title: Parachute Components Drag
spec: Write a function `deploy(components)` that calculates the drag coefficient of a deployed parachute system. The input is a list of strings with a component name and its size or quantity. Create separate structural elements for each item. A canopy contributes its size multiplied by zero point eight to the drag. Lines contribute their length multiplied by zero point zero one. A riser contributes its quantity multiplied by zero point zero five. A pilot contributes a flat two point zero to the drag, regardless of size. Sum the individual drag contributions and return the total float value. Example: the list ["canopy 100", "lines 200"] results in eighty two point zero.

title: Cave Formations Age
spec: Write a function `survey(formations)` that estimates the age in centuries of a discovered cavern based on its mineral deposits. The input is a list of strings describing a formation type and its height or area in centimeters. Instantiate specific geological models for each formation. A stalactite takes two centuries per centimeter to form. A stalagmite takes three centuries per centimeter. A column takes four centuries per centimeter. A flowstone takes one century per centimeter. Find the formation that yields the highest estimated age, and return that maximum integer age. Example: the input ["stalactite 50", "stalagmite 40"] evaluates to one hundred centuries.

title: Kite Flying Lift
spec: Write a function `fly(kites)` that calculates the total lift force in newtons generated by a collection of tethered kites. The input is a list of strings, each specifying a kite style and the wind speed in kilometers per hour. Handle each style with a dedicated aerodynamic object. A box kite generates lift equal to the wind speed multiplied by one point five. A delta kite generates lift equal to the wind speed multiplied by two point zero. A diamond kite generates lift equal to the wind speed multiplied by zero point eight. A foil kite generates lift equal to the wind speed multiplied by three point zero. Sum the lift forces and return the float total. Example: the input ["delta 10", "diamond 10"] computes to twenty eight point zero.

title: Bookbinding Materials Weight
spec: Write a function `bind(materials)` that calculates the weight in grams of a custom bound book. The input is a list of strings with a material type and its quantity or length. Create dedicated material instances for each item. Leather adds two hundred grams per unit. Paper adds five grams per sheet. Thread adds one gram per unit of length. Glue adds two grams per unit of volume. Sum the weights contributed by all materials and return the integer total. Example: the input ["leather 1", "paper 50"] totals four hundred fifty.

title: Paint Mixing Drying Time
spec: Write a function `paint(pigments)` that calculates the total drying time in hours for a custom mixed color. The input is a list of strings containing a pigment or medium type and its volume in milliliters. Route each component to its own property calculator. A red pigment takes two hours per milliliter to dry. A blue pigment takes three hours per milliliter. A white pigment takes one point five hours per milliliter. A medium takes zero point five hours per milliliter. Average the drying times of all items by dividing the sum of their individual drying times by the total volume of all components. Return the float average. Example: the input ["red 10", "blue 10"] returns two point five.

title: Bicycle Gears Maintenance
spec: Write a function `pedal(components)` that estimates the total maintenance time in minutes for overhauling a bicycle drivetrain. The input is a list of strings detailing a component and its quantity or length. Process each component by instantiating its own structural model. A derailleur takes forty five minutes per unit to service. A cassette takes twenty minutes per unit. A chain takes one minute per link of length. A shifter takes fifteen minutes per unit. Add up the maintenance time for all specified parts and return the integer total. Example: the input ["cassette 1", "chain 50"] outputs seventy.

title: Custom Keyboard Assembler
spec: Write an object-oriented simulation to calculate the total latency and cost of a mechanical keyboard build. The entry function `assemble(parts)` receives a list of tuples containing a part type string and its numerical specifications. Instantiate objects for a key switch, a key cap, a circuit board, and a case frame based on the part type. A key switch calculates latency as travel distance divided by spring force. A key cap adds zero latency but has a cost based on its profile height. A circuit board has a fixed latency of two milliseconds plus one per diode. A case frame adds a base cost based on its metal density. Sum the individual properties and return a tuple of the total latency and total cost. For example, processing a list with one key switch of distance four and force two, and one case frame costing fifty, returns a total latency of two and a cost of fifty.

title: Bonsai Shape Evaluator
spec: Determine the final aesthetic score of a miniature tree by processing a sequence of pruning actions. The function `prune(actions)` takes a list of instruction tuples. Create distinct entity objects for a branch node, a root ball, a foliage pad, and a wire tie. A branch node increases the score by its length divided by its thickness. A root ball provides a base score equal to its spread minus depth. A foliage pad adds points equal to its leaf density. A wire tie deducts points if applied for too long based on its metal gauge. Iterate through the actions, construct the appropriate entity, and accumulate their scores. Return the final integer score. Example: a root ball with spread ten and depth five, plus a foliage pad with density three, results in a score of eight.

title: Snowboard Binding Configurator
spec: Calculate the responsiveness rating and weight of a snowboard setup. The function `configure(components)` processes a list of raw component data tuples. Represent the gear using distinct classes for a high back, an ankle strap, a toe cap, and a base plate. A high back contributes stiffness multiplied by its forward lean angle. An ankle strap adds cushioning divided by flexibility. A toe cap contributes a flat grip rating. A base plate dampens vibrations, improving the overall ride score by a fixed amount per millimeter of thickness. Instantiate each component from the data, sum their individual responsiveness scores, and apply a ten percent penalty if the total weight exceeds a given threshold. Return the final rounded rating. Example: a high back with stiffness five and lean two, paired with a three-millimeter base plate, adds thirteen to the total rating.

title: Surfboard Volume Calculator
spec: Estimate the buoyancy of a custom surfboard by aggregating its layers. The entry function `shape(measurements)` accepts a list of material dimensions. Model the board using objects for a foam blank, a stringer spine, a fiberglass coat, and a fin box. A foam blank calculates volume using length, width, and thickness. A stringer spine deducts a small volume based on its wood density and width. A fiberglass coat adds weight which inversely affects the final buoyancy score. A fin box deducts a fixed buoyancy but adds a stability multiplier. Build the respective objects, compute their specific volume and weight contributions, and return the final net buoyancy. Example: a foam blank of volume fifty and a stringer spine reducing it by two returns forty eight.

title: Vinyl Pressing Simulator
spec: Simulate the manufacturing quality of a vinyl record. The function `press(stages)` processes a sequence of production steps. Use separate objects to represent a lacquer disc, a stamper plate, a vinyl pellet, and a center label. A lacquer disc sets the base audio fidelity based on groove depth. A stamper plate reduces fidelity slightly by its wear count multiplied by a wear factor. A vinyl pellet adds surface noise depending on its color additive percentage. A center label does not affect audio but adds a static visual appeal score. Create each stage object, evaluate its fidelity modifier, and return a tuple of the final audio quality percentage and visual appeal. Example: a lacquer disc starting at one hundred, hit by a stamper plate with two wear points, results in an audio quality of ninety eight.

title: Hot Air Balloon Lift
spec: Determine if a hot air balloon can achieve liftoff by comparing lift force to total weight. The function `ascend(parts)` takes a list of balloon section properties. Create specific objects for an envelope fabric, a burner unit, a wicker basket, and a tether rope. An envelope fabric provides lift based on its volume and the internal temperature minus outside temperature. A burner unit adds significant weight but dictates the temperature capability. A wicker basket adds base weight plus passenger weight. A tether rope limits the maximum altitude regardless of lift and adds drag. Instantiate the parts, sum the total lift and total weight, and return true if lift exceeds weight by at least ten percent. Example: lift of five hundred and weight of four hundred returns a boolean true.

title: Scuba Dive Duration
spec: Estimate the maximum bottom time for a diver based on their equipment loadout. The function `dive(equipment)` accepts a list of gear specifications. Represent the setup with objects for an air tank, a regulator valve, a buoyancy compensator, and a weight belt. An air tank holds a specific volume of pressurized breathing gas. A regulator valve determines the flow rate per minute based on depth. A buoyancy compensator adds drag which increases the diver exertion rate, effectively multiplying the flow rate. A weight belt adds static negative buoyancy requiring more physical effort. Instantiate the objects, calculate the effective gas consumption rate, and return the maximum minutes the diver can stay submerged. Example: an air tank with two thousand units and an effective flow rate of fifty yields forty minutes.

title: Lathe Spindle Turning
spec: Calculate the final diameter and surface finish of a wooden table leg. The function `turn(operations)` takes a list of cutting tools and their pass depths. Model the process using distinct objects for a spindle gouge, a roughing gouge, a parting tool, and a skew chisel. A roughing gouge removes material quickly but leaves a rough finish penalty. A spindle gouge removes less material but improves the finish score. A parting tool makes deep narrow cuts without affecting overall finish. A skew chisel provides a massive finish bonus but removes very little diameter. Build the tool objects from the operations list, apply their effects sequentially to a starting diameter of ten, and return a tuple of the final diameter and finish score.

title: Kiln Firing Schedule
spec: Compute the total energy required to fire a batch of ceramics. The function `fire(contents)` processes a list of items loaded into the oven. Use objects to represent a clay body, a glaze coat, a kiln shelf, and a pyrometric cone. A clay body requires energy proportional to its mass and its specific curing temperature. A glaze coat needs a quick spike in energy based on its flux percentage. A kiln shelf absorbs ambient heat, adding a fixed energy tax per square inch. A pyrometric cone acts as an energy cutoff, halting further energy addition once its specific heat work rating is reached. Instantiate the loaded items, calculate the thermal energy for each up to the cutoff, and return the sum. Example: a clay body needing five hundred units and a shelf taxing fifty units returns five hundred fifty.

title: Coil Machine Tuner
spec: Evaluate the running frequency and duty cycle of a magnetic tattoo machine. The function `tune(settings)` receives component specifications. Construct objects for an armature bar, a contact screw, an electromagnetic coil, and a tube grip. An armature bar lowers the frequency based on its raw weight. A contact screw alters the duty cycle based on its gap distance in millimeters. An electromagnetic coil increases frequency based on its number of wire wraps. A tube grip absorbs vibrations, lowering the effective running frequency by a static percentage. Create the components, compute the final speed in hertz and the duty cycle percentage, and return them as a tuple. Example: a ten wrap coil with a heavy bar might yield one hundred hertz and a fifty percent cycle.

title: Cobbler Boot Assembly
spec: Determine the durability rating and weight of a handcrafted boot. The function `assemble(materials)` reads a list of construction elements. Model the footwear using objects for a leather upper, a rubber sole, a heel block, and a steel toe. A leather upper provides durability based on hide thickness minus a stretch factor. A rubber sole adds significant weight but provides high abrasion resistance. A heel block adds base weight and a fixed structural posture bonus. A steel toe adds immense durability at the cost of extremely high weight. Instantiate the materials, aggregate their weight and durability values, and return them as a tuple. Example: an upper with ten durability and a sole with twenty yields thirty total durability.

title: Lock Cylinder Picker
spec: Simulate the difficulty of picking a pin tumbler lock. The entry function `pick(chamber)` takes a list of internal lock components. Represent the mechanism using objects for a key pin, a driver pin, a tension wrench, and a cylinder core. A key pin adds difficulty based on its length variation from the adjacent pin. A driver pin adds difficulty if it features security serrations. A tension wrench reduces overall difficulty depending on its flex rating. A cylinder core sets the base friction difficulty before pins are factored in. Instantiate the parts, sum the individual pin difficulties over the core base, apply the wrench reduction, and return the final integer difficulty score.

title: Typewriter Kinematics
spec: Calculate the typing speed limit and ink consumption of a restored vintage typewriter. The function `typewrite(strokes)` processes a sequence of mechanical parts involved in a keystroke. Use distinct objects for a type bar, a carriage roller, a ribbon spool, and a shift key. A type bar determines the minimum millisecond delay between strokes based on its return spring tension. A carriage roller adds a friction delay per character. A ribbon spool consumes a set amount of ink per strike. A shift key doubles the tension delay temporarily for capital letters. Build the components, find the maximum delay to determine words per minute, and return the speed and total ink used as a tuple.

title: Harmonica Pitch Bender
spec: Evaluate the resonant frequencies produced by a diatonic harmonica. The function `bend(notes)` accepts a sequence of breath inputs. Create structures for a blow reed, a draw reed, a comb plate, and a cover plate. A blow reed produces a static pitch that shifts slightly based on breath force. A draw reed allows significant pitch bending down depending on negative pressure. A comb plate acts as a resonator, adding a volume multiplier based on its material density. A cover plate muffles the high frequencies, acting as a dampener multiplier. Instantiate the parts, process the breath sequence to find the final pitch and volume of each note, and return a list of tuples.

title: Spin Time Estimator
spec: Estimate the maximum sleep time of a custom throw toy. The function `spin(parts)` processes the physical traits of the build. Model the setup using objects for an axle bearing, a string loop, a plastic body, and a response pad. An axle bearing reduces friction based on its ball count and lubrication viscosity. A string loop causes a constant deceleration drag. A plastic body determines the initial angular momentum based on its rim weight distribution. A response pad increases friction sharply at low speeds to return the toy earlier. Instantiate each part, calculate the initial spin speed minus the combined friction and drag over time, and return the total seconds until it stops.

title: Saponification Value
spec: Calculate the final lye concentration and curing time for a cold process soap batch. The function `saponify(ingredients)` takes a list of recipe components. Use objects to represent a lye solution, a base oil, a fragrance blend, and a color pigment. A lye solution provides the active chemical mass. A base oil neutralizes a specific amount of lye based on its saponification index and adds to the curing days. A fragrance blend accelerates the curing time if it contains alcohol. A color pigment absorbs a tiny fraction of the oil without affecting the lye. Create the ingredient objects, compute the remaining unreacted lye and the final cure time in days, returning both as a tuple.

title: Glass Window Structural
spec: Assess the structural integrity and light transmission of a decorative window panel. The function `solder(panel)` processes a list of panel elements. Represent the artwork using objects for a glass piece, a lead came, a solder joint, and a zinc border. A glass piece transmits light based on its color opacity but adds weight. A lead came provides structural rigidity based on its profile width but blocks light completely. A solder joint acts as a weak point, deducting from the integrity score depending on its surface area. A zinc border provides a flat structural integrity bonus to the entire perimeter. Instantiate the elements, sum the total integrity and light transmission, and return them.

title: Wallet Thickness Profiler
spec: Calculate the empty thickness and card capacity of a minimalist wallet design. The function `profile(layers)` accepts a sequence of construction steps. Model the assembly using objects for a card slot, a cash pocket, a thread stitch, and an edge paint. A card slot adds a specific millimeter thickness and increases capacity by a designated number of cards. A cash pocket adds double thickness but holds no cards.
